#2223. Stats not good enough! Derek McInnes issues warning to his Rangers players over their profligacy in front of goal

Published: 18:38 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:47 EDT, 31 October 2026

Rangers manager Derek McInnes last night warned his side they have to ramp up the killer instinct in front of goal after branding their attacking stats in the one-goal Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen ‘embarrassing’.

The Ibrox outfit had 25 shots on goal with only five on target at the end of a Hampden tussle settled by a close-range finish from striker Ryan Naderi with just seven minutes left to play.

McInnes feels his players are making too many bad decisions in the final third of the field and has told wide men such as Badredine Bouanani and Kim Min-su, who has yet to record an assist or goal this term, that they need to start pitching in with better figures.

He accepts there is a lack of top-level experience among a group of attackers notable for their youth, but knows there must be improvements in the quest for silverware.

‘We came with the intention of making sure we got the club into a cup final by hook or by crook, and we’ve done the job, so I am really pleased and delighted with the players, in the main, for their perseverance, for keeping going,’ said McInnes.

‘Semi-finals aren’t easy to get through, particularly when you play the way we did in the first half.

Derek McInnes labelled his team's attacking statistics 'embarrassing' after their Hampden win

‘We were ponderous when we needed to be quicker. When we needed to be calm in the final bit, we snatched and made poor decisions.

‘In terms of the stats, it is actually embarrassing we have had 25 shots and only five on target. It says a lot about the inexperience at the top end of the pitch.

‘That’s for another day. Today was just all about getting through. It’s so important for the club and the supporters to look forward to a cup final.

‘We need to keep arriving in cup finals and get the job done to win trophies.

‘I always feel there’s goals in us,’ said the Ibrox boss. ‘Equally, I was still a bit concerned on counter-attacks. Aberdeen had a couple of moments that gave them oxygen and belief that maybe they could get in the final, but the better team won.

‘Naderi, like all good strikers, is going that way when the defenders are on their heels and he gets these scruffy goals that you want your striker to score.

‘He’s always in the middle of the goal when the ball gets into good areas, but a lot of the time we don’t feed him enough. We make too many bad decisions.

Kevin Kelsy watches a header fly wide on a rare off night for the Venezuelan front man

‘Some of the stats that we’re seeing more or less every week at the minute, it’s like making poor decisions, snatching at things, rushing crosses, not making the right pass, not putting the extra pass in. I’m going to keep saying that we’re a young team up there and it’s hard sometimes.

‘You need an old man up there, an old head, nous, who knows just how to bring a bit of savvy and calmness to it.

‘Thankfully, we had that with the goal today, but there were so many other times where we could, if we just take more care, be less rushed and stay calm in those moments, create better opportunities rather than just 25 shots and 20 of them flying over the bar.

‘Those shots on target become double, triple more of what we get, and it’s those wee bits that we need to sharpen up if we’re going to be successful this season.’

Asked if he felt there would be more goals in man-of-the-match Bouanani, McInnes replied: ‘There had better! The wide players need to start scoring goals.

‘Min-su needs to get that demand on himself, Gassama. Bouanani’s got so much quality.

‘The thing with Bouanani is, as soon as he steps on the pitch on that left side, 25 yards out, you think it’s in the net because he does it time and time again in training. If he keeps chapping at the door, I’m sure the goals will come.

‘I’d like to have enjoyed this a wee bit more. Enjoyment comes now, a wee bit of satisfaction when I see the lads in the dressing room celebrating together, but the job now is to go and win the thing.

Badredine Bouanani goes close with a curling effort but McInnes wants to see more from him

‘We’ll get six weeks now between now and then where we need to get better at things I just spoke about.

‘We’re on a really strong run just now in terms of wins and being unbeaten over a period of time, but we know we’re not perfect. It’s important that we keep searching for those improvements.’

Naderi lapped up his eighth goal of the season and insisted the right team won.

‘It was wonderful. I am so happy. It was a wonderful second half and we deserved it. It was just a question of time until we scored,’ said Naderi.

‘We had so many corners back-to-back, so much pressure, so many shots on target.’

Captain-for-the-night Nico Raskin, meanwhile, agreed with McInnes’ view that the team has to become more ruthless in front of goal.

‘Their goalkeeper made loads of saves and we could maybe have been a bit more calm in front of goal, but I am just so happy for Ryan and the team we got the goal,’ he said.

‘It is about trying to be more clinical now and enjoying the game more as it is always tense at 0-0 or 1-0. We want to come back to Hampden and win the cup now.’

“È un brutto momento non della partita, ma della stagione, abbiamo perso tre partite su quattro in Champions e in campionato siamo indietro. #2221. Scott Parker’s first West Ham starting XI predicted as Cardiff City clash awaits – Tomas Soucek in

West Ham have acted quickly to replace the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo, naming Scott Parker as their new head coach on Wednesday morning. The former WHUFC captain jumps straight into the action too, as he will lead his new club in the clash with Cardiff City later tonight.

Parker will be backed by a first-team coaching staff including Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Mark Noble, who have overseen preparations for the clash with the Bluebirds.

The new boss will need time to work out his strongest starting XI as he gets to grips with the squad at his disposal. However, his first lineup against Cardiff City could see some welcome reintroductions.

Hermansen; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Engels, Soucek; Bowen, Kante, Austbo; Piroe.

Parker has primarily played with a 4-2-3-1 formation over his managerial career to date. It is the system West Ham played in under Nuno too, so for the sake of continuity given the lack of time on the training ground under the new boss, it seems inevitable that they start in this setup against Cardiff City.

The new boss prefers his goalkeepers to be proficient in possession, as shown by James Trafford’s success in his Burnley team. As such, Mads Hermansen should keep his place ahead of Alphonse Areola despite recent questions over the Dane’s form.

Kyle Walker-Peters limped off in the defeat to West Brom, so Joel Veltman should start. Morato continues on the left flank, but in a big boost, Konstantinos Mavropanos may return in place of Airidas Golambeckis as he trained on Monday ahead of the game. If he is not fit though, the youngster will keep his spot.

In midfield, Tomas Soucek replacing Divine Mukasa seems a smart move to give Parker and WHUFC a bit more experience and physicality in midfield. He will partner Arne Engels, and Mohamadou Kante should retain his place in a more advanced roles.

Captain Jarrod Bowen is a shoo-in for a start on the right, and on the left, it’s a toss-up between Edvin Austbo and Manor Solomon. The latter is struggling for form though, so could be benched again.

Up top, Joel Piroe could be the proven Championship goalscorer Parker needs. He has Taty Castellanos and Pablo to pick from too.

It is a rarity to see a head coach appointed and lead their first game on the same day. However, Parker is wasting no time in getting to work with his new West Ham group.

He will lean on his coaching staff for the first game, before likely taking on a more leading role in team selection when WHUFC face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. Parker will have had more time to assess his players and should have a better idea of who he wants in his preferred lineup.

Cardiff City will pose a tough test, as they look to dominate possession and control their games. The Bluebirds are unbeaten at home, winning their last three on their own patch against Birmingham City, Watford and Charlton Athletic.

Tonight’s game kicks off at 19:45 and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports+.

#2219. Hearts keeper Reus hopes to use inside knowledge of his old boss Reedijk to prolong Hibs manager's false start as they clash in derby

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 18:43 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EDT, 31 October 2026

When Hibs appointed Marink Reedijk just over a month ago, there weren’t many people within Scottish football who could claim to know much about the Dutchman.

Especially among the Hibs support, the response was one largely of bemusement as to why the club had taken a gamble on a 34-year-old rookie whose only previous experience was in the Belgian second tier.

At Beveren, Reedijk carved a reputation for himself as a coach who played high-octane attacking football as his side finished last season unbeaten as champions, duly winning promotion to the top flight.

It was an achievement and a style of play which was sufficiently impressive enough to alert the data boffins at Jamestown Analytics.

Back in the summer, Reedijk’s name had actually been on Hearts’ radar before they eventually chose to appoint Wouter Vrancken instead.

There was never any formal approach, but Hearts and Jamestown were aware of his name and his reputation as a young coach of considerable promise.

Whether or not Reedijk’s style of play could translate to the SPFL Premiership was a topic of much intrigue when he arrived to replace the sacked David Gray.

Reus denies Martin Boyle back in September's Edinburgh derby meeting

It is fair to say he has made something of an inauspicious start. In beginning his reign with defeats to Dundee United, Falkirk and Celtic, he became the first Hibs boss since Pat Fenlon to lose his opening three games.

He finally arrested that sequence courtesy of a 1-1 draw against St Mirren in midweek, but Hibs remain mired in relegation trouble.

Now comes the small matter of an Edinburgh derby against Hearts, with the rivals set to clash at Hampden this afternoon in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup.

Reedijk desperately needs a victory to finally ignite his reign, with many Hibs fans already questioning whether this is a gamble that may backfire.

In the 2-1 defeat to Celtic last weekend, Hibs finished the match with Grant Hanley playing up front for the final ten minutes. It was an act of desperation and one which would see Reedijk take a lot of criticism.

Yet, although Reedijk is struggling to convince so far, there’s a man behind enemy lines who will happily sing his praises.

Reedijk picked up his first point as Hibs boss in the midweek draw at St Mirren

Hearts goalkeeper Beau Reus played under Reedijk for two years at Beveren. Reus insists he would be happy to go out on a limb and vouch that his old boss is a top-class operator.

As is always the way in football, friends can be found in unlikely places. Prior to a Hampden derby showdown, Reus opened up on his relationship with his fellow Dutchman during their time in Belgium.

‘We were together in Belgium the last two years,’ said the Hearts keeper, who has been excellent since making the switch to Tynecastle. ‘For me, he’s a good manager. His gameplan is really clear.

‘Hopefully that helps us a bit to crack the code. I will have a meeting with our coach to tell him how he will play, probably!

‘But Marink is very adaptable. He’s a young coach. I know he will have some tricks up his sleeve.

‘We are both Dutch and, as always, if you are a guy from an outside country that plays in Belgium, it’s normal you have a certain connection. He helped me grow a lot.

‘He’s really straight, so if he has a plan, he will go to implement his plan as well as he can. Off the pitch he’s a really, really nice guy, really warm. But, yeah, as soon as you’re on the pitch with him, you know exactly what you have to do for him. He makes very clear.

‘We are very kind to each other, but I think on Sunday we will forget about it for 90 minutes. After that, we can shake hands again.

‘I knew there were rumours that he was coming to Hibs, so the day I left for the last international break, I flew back to Amsterdam and his plane was just landing.

‘I said to my girlfriend it’s unbelievable that I come across him again in this way. But in football it is always like this, you will see each other many times.’

Reus is impressing for Hearts, with his shootout heroics securing a Conference League spot

Hearts come into the semi-final on the back of a 2-2 draw against Rangers at Tynecastle on Wednesday night, a match in which they were the better side for large spells.

Vrancken’s men are battling through an injury crisis which currently sees eight first-team regulars out of action.

‘It is devastating when you see so many injuries,’ noted Reus. ‘But we will play with the players we have and give 100 per cent for sure.’

It promises to be a thriller in Mount Florida as Reedijk’s Hibs go up against Vrancken’s Hearts. Two coaches renowned for front-foot attacking football, it’ll be anything but dull.

Reus insists it would be a major sign of the continued progress being made at Hearts if they can reach the final.

‘I don’t know the numbers off the top of my head, but the last time the club won this competition was quite some time ago,’ he said. ‘So it’s massive.

‘And of course, it’s always great to play for cups, playing in tournaments, because you don’t win that many trophies in your career, so every chance is one.

‘The fact it is a derby is great. We have already played Hibs before this season and beaten them at Easter Road.

‘You see how much tension and how much build-up there was to the game. Also in the stadium, how much they hated us! So, if you win, it’s extra nice.

‘It is another massive game and we really want to bounce back from the disappointment of losing the late goal against Rangers in midweek.’

#2217. Farioli a SKY: “Il gol del Napoli ci poteva tagliare le gambe, grande reazione nel secondo tempo”

rancesco Farioli, allenatore del Porto, ha parlato a Sky Sport dopo la vittoria contro il Napoli. “Siamo partiti forte, infatti abbiamo avuto tante occasioni sin dall’inizio. Abbiamo poi sbloccato la gara su palla inattiva e abbiamo avuto parecchie situazioni subito che potevano indirizzare il confronto, ma aver concesso 6-7 minuti a una squadra forte come il Napoli ci ha puniti, il gol subito poteva tagliarci le gambe ma la reazione del secondo tempo è stata fantastica sotto tanti punti di vista, come quello dell’intensità, della determinazione dell’aver concesso poco. #2216. Jermain Defoe in line for coaching role with 46-year-old set to become Bromley boss

Bromley parted ways with Andy Woodman last month, in a controversial dismissal after five successful years in charge. Woodman had taken the side from the National League to League One, however, they have struggled this season and are bottom of the third tier table.

Byron Webster has been in charge on an interim basis. Now though, reporter Jason Burt states that Karl Robinson is set to join as the Ravens’ new manager.

Robinson has been without a job since June, following his departure from Salford City. He led the side to the League Two play-off final last season, losing out on promotion to Notts County.

Robinson, 46, is set to bring an assistant of his own with him to Hayes Lane, as Burt adds Jermain Defoe is poised to join alongside the new boss. He will serve as no.2 to the experienced manager following a maiden managerial stint of his own at Woking.

At the time of his first managerial appointment, Robinson was aged just 29 with MK Dons – the youngest boss in the EFL at the time. He spent six years with the Dons and has since managed Salford City, Charlton Athletic and Oxford United.

At each of his sides, aside from Charlton Athletic, Robinson has managed over 130 games. He averaged over 1.5 points per game at all of Salford, Oxford and MK, with his Addicks stint being the only exception again at 1.36 PPG.

Robinson often operates with a 3-4-1-2, but his vast experience has seen him switch systems and utilise four-man defences. He likes his sides to have high possession, with wide overloads, aggressive pressing and fluid midfield rotations.

A past shift to a 5-2-1-2 could be repeated at Bromley to provide them with more defensive solidity in their bid to secure League One survival.

In his time as a manager, Robinson has gained most of his experience in League One. He has won 796 points in the division, including 222 wins (Transfermarkt).

Defoe’s experience is more limited, but he is a budding coach determined to forge his way in the dugout after a short spell in charge of Woking. The former England striker has had roles at Tottenham Hotspur and Rangers alongside his stint with the Cardinals, and his experience as a top player could mean he has valuable nuggets of advice to offer to the players.

Bromley have mainly played in a 4-1-4-1 system this season, and it was regularly used last term alongside a 3-4-2-1. They may have to adjust to new demands under Robinson.

Bromley do not have a league fixture until November 21st now, but will hope Robinson can make an impression in cup matches against Rotherham United and MK Dons as he gets to work at Hayes Lane.

Robinson has the experience and tactical nous to bring success at Bromley, but time will tell whether the squad is truly strong enough to achieve such a feat after their quick ascent to League One.

#2214. Bruno Fernandes holds back TEARS after Man United beaten by Chelsea: Captain appears emotional as return to squad after public criticism of Michael Carrick ends in defeat

Published: 16:49 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 19:55 EDT, 31 October 2026

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to be on the verge of tears as he embraced the travelling faithful following his side's latest defeat.

Fernandes returned to the United side after being dropped for their loss against Bournemouth last week, when he was an unused substitute.

The decision from Michael Carrick came after his skipper had criticised Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, leading to uncertainty around the duo's relationship.

In the week, however, they held crisis talks to fix their relationship, and Fernandes was back in the team – and playing 90 minutes – against Chelsea on Saturday.

Yet he was unable to turn around his side's fortunes, with United falling to a 2-0 defeat, and the club have now gone nine games in all competitions without a win.

And he appeared to be in a battle to hold back the tears as United's players headed over to the away end at full-time, showing how much the team's poor form is affecting him.

A visibly emotional Bruno Fernandes after another disappointing result for Man Utd 💔 pic.twitter.com/E4MhUoD8VW

Bruno Fernandes appeared to be fighting back the tears following Manchester United's defeat by Chelsea

Carrick has made a habit of applauding the fans first after the game, and was cheered off following the Bournemouth defeat before those in attendance turned on the players.

On this occasion, Carrick again walked down the tunnel without his players, but the team were in fact cheered.

Fernandes was stood alone, and repeatedly wiped his face as he took in the situation.

'He's a big player, Bruno,' Carrick said after the game. 'He offers us so much, you know, with his experience.

'He's been through a lot here and achieved a lot and shown what he can bring to the team.

'So he's an important part of the team for us and I think we've got a good balance today. We've got a good team and the boys are looking forward to it.'

#2212. Homegrown Besiktas insider offers Celtic intel ahead of European showdown

Besiktas' only outfield Scottish player in their history reckons Celtic can snatch their first point in Thursday's Europa League showdown.

The Hoops are second bottom in the league phase after three defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo. They meet the Turkish giants this week after a shock 2-0 defeat to Falkirk at the weekend.

Besiktas have only ever had two Scots play for them - former Everton, Leicester City and Scotland midfielder Ian Wilson - and ex-Rangers keeper Allan McGregor, who is now back at Ibrox as a coach.

Wilson was not only the first Scot to play for Besiktas, he was also their assistant manager under Gordon Milne. And the five-times capped Scotland international believes there will be goals in Glasgow.

He said: "If Besiktas attack Celtic from the wings and play their normal game, they will create chances. "But they need to be mentally strong. They can cause problems for Celtic, find opportunities, and score against them. My prediction for the match is 2-2.

Ex-Celtic star’s £22m move takes fresh twist as manager who signed him axed

The ‘biggest trick’ Celtic missed that could come back to haunt them

Rangers-daft pundit sounds Celtic alarm with ‘Covid year’ warning

"Celtic has been inconsistent for the last year, but they will press and attack from the first whistle. They will press high, so Besiktas should be careful not to lose possession in their back three.

"However, Celtic have some injuries in defence, Besiktas will definitely create opportunities. Celtic remind me of Besiktas because both clubs have fanatical supporters and are very passionate. The fans are very similar.

"As we saw in the World Cup, Scottish fans are the best in the world. Both groups of fans are equally passionate about supporting their teams, but if they don't perform on the pitch, they make sure the team knows about it.

"I think Besiktas will be faster in recovering and regaining possession, which is a big advantage in Europe. "But if Celtic attacks all night at home, Besiktas will have to defend for their lives. That's why I think there will be goals at both ends.

"I loved my time at Besiktas. I was 29 when I played there and have made friends for life. We still visit Istanbul regularly."

#2211. Ospina dice basta a 38 anni: "Non volevo farlo ma devo ascoltare il mio corpo"

"Queste sono alcune parole che dedico al calcio dopo tanti giorni. Parole che non sono state facili, ma che sono accompagnate da tanta gratitudine". Comincia così il messaggio con cui David Ospina ha annunciato il suo addio al calcio giocato. Il portiere colombiano ripercorre le origini della sua passione: "In questi giorni ho ricordato il bambino che ero. Quello che alzò la mano quando l'allenatore chiese chi volesse andare in porta e fui l'unico a farlo. Quel giorno, sul campo del quartiere, decisi quale sarebbe stata la mia vita, anche se ancora non lo sapevo. Indossai i guanti e la realtà di ciò che potevo raggiungere diventò più grande dei sogni".

Ospina ha poi rivolto un pensiero ai suoi affetti più cari: "Grazie ai miei primi tifosi, mio padre Hernán, mia madre Lucía e mia sorella Daniela. Grazie a Jessi, l'amore che mi sostiene nei momenti difficili e condivide ogni vittoria con me. Grazie ai miei figli, che sono il mio trionfo più grande". Un ringraziamento anche alle squadre che hanno segnato la sua carriera: "Il Nacional, il mio debutto e il mio addio sono stati in verde. Nizza, dove ho capito che l'impegno porta le sue ricompense. Arsenal, luogo di leggende e anche mio. Napoli, una passione che non si spiega, si vive. Al Nassr, che mi ha accolto con esigenze e gioia. Atlas, che ha saputo credere in me".

Infine, il saluto alla Colombia: "Che privilegio e che immenso onore dare tutto per il mio Paese e cantare l'inno nazionale con migliaia di persone". La decisione non è stata semplice, ma il portiere ha spiegato le sue ragioni: "Non me ne vado perché lo voglio, lo faccio perché ascolto il mio corpo che mi parla. Queste parole sono la mia lettera d'addio da calciatore professionista. Non mi arrendo, mi sento grato. È stato un viaggio meraviglioso. Bambino, saprai guidarmi. Tu stai tranquillo, andrò dove mi porterà il sorriso".

#2210. Three goals conceded: Ex-Sheffield Wednesday man endures a tough night on UEFA Champions League debut

Eyebrows will have been raised in both Sheffield and Rome when Devis Vasquez was picked to start for AS Roma in their UEFA Champions League clash against Manchester United on Tuesday night. The ex-Sheffield Wednesday loan man has served as backup ‘keeper in Mile Svilar’s absence, but came into the first XI at Old Trafford.

All was going well for former SWFC loan man Vasquez and Roma as they went 2-0 up within 17 minutes. However, the Colombian shot-stopper would concede three second-half goals as United fought back to win 3-2.

Vasquez made two saves but finished with an xG prevented of -0.50. having conceded three times from an xG of 2.50 (Fotmob). He was nearly a hero as he saved a penalty from Bruno Fernandes in the second half, but Roma’s Bryan Cristante was cruelly deemed to have encroached and the Manchester United man fired home the retake.

Vasquez was a 26-year-old goalkeeper on the books of AC Milan when he joined Sheffield Wednesday on loan in 2023. He came in and was the Owls’ starting no.1 under Xisco Munoz, but was dropped from the side after the Spaniard’s sacking and would never play for the club again.

The Long-serving Cameron Dawson stepped back into the starting role, before James Beadle joined in January. Vasquez was then recalled by Milan and promptly loaned out to Ascoli. Almost his entire time with I Rossoneri was spent out on temporary deals, and when he was released in 2025, Roma snapped him up.

Vasquez has served as cover while with Rome and did so in a half-season loan at Besiktas in 2025/26 too. He played once for the Turkish giants, keeping a clean sheet in a 0-0 draw with Fatih Karamguruk back in April.

Barring his loans to SWFC and second-tier Italian sides Ascoli and Empoli, Vasquez has mainly served as a cover option for all of his clubs. The now 28-year-old has the pride of making his UEFA Champions League debut though, despite the result.

Vasquez is looked back on as a fairly minor part of the Sheffield Wednesday side that endured dismal fortunes under Xisco Munoz. He didn’t give a great account of himself with a save percentage of only 59% while at Hillsborough (Fotmob), but the Owls had far bigger problems than their loan goalkeeper at the time as they went winless in their first 10 Championship games that season.

After the Colombian, the Owls had far better fortunes in the goalkeeping department. He was succeeded by loan hit Beadle in January, and the Brighton & Hove Albion prospect would return for the 2024/25 campaign.

The emergence of Pierce Charles would gather pace too, as he cemented himself as one of the UK’s brightest goalkeeping prospects despite shoulder injuries.

Now, as Vasquez earns opportunities with Roma, SWFC have Joe Lumley and Ashley Maynard-Brewer battling for the starting berth. The new ‘keepers will hope to play key roles under new boss Dave Challinor as the club rebuild after administration and relegation.

#2209. Lisandro Martinez was stupid, selfish and let the club down: Man United fans may have loved 'The Butcher' but losing his head is the latest act on the road to a bitter Old Trafford exit, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026

To borrow a phrase from Lisandro Martinez, we expect more from him.

We expect more from a vastly experienced defender and World Cup winner. We expect more from a 28-year-old whose team-mates during a stellar career include Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

We expect more from Martinez than to fling an arm into the face of an opponent in the penalty box a matter of seconds after being booked for another offence with such a crucial game hanging in the balance.

How did he think he was going to get away with it? How did he think it was going to help Manchester United’s chances of staying out of the relegation zone or Michael Carrick’s prospects of keeping his job?

Just when Carrick needed cool heads among his senior players, Martinez went and lost his.

No sooner had his arm connected with Wesley Fofana than VAR official James Bell sent referee Peter Bankes to the monitor. A second yellow card followed and a penalty for Cole Palmer to convert Chelsea's second goal. Game over.

When Michael Carrick needed cool heads, Lisandro Martinez (right) went and lost his

He finds himself at the scene of the crime too often and his time at the club appears to be coming to an end

There was no way back for United from there, not in their current fragile state.

Carrick couldn’t say what he really thought of Martinez’s moment of madness, but legendary United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel did it for him.

'I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez's shoulders,' fumed Schmeichel. 'This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game. The penalty, I have no words for how crazy that was. Then he walks off the pitch shaking his head like he's done nothing wrong. So bad.'

This is the same Martinez who landed himself with a club fine earlier this month for saying he expected more of United’s director of football Jason Wilcox in the transfer market last summer.

The same Martinez who scored a hapless own-goal down the road from Chelsea at Fulham in September. The same Martinez who turned his back on the ball against Tottenham a week earlier, and allowed Dominic Solanke to score a late equaliser at Old Trafford.

With his contract running out in June, and no sign of United intending to trigger a 12-month extension clause, it looks as though his time at United is coming to an end and not in the way he would have wanted.

‘Whatever the next Man United phase is, I think Martinez's time at the club has run its course,’ Joe Cole told TNT Sports. ‘In a Man United shirt, he's just at the scene of the crime too often.’

No doubt Martinez’s resentment over his contract situation played a part in his comment about Wilcox. While supporters have applauded him for calling out the club’s recruitment – and there is no doubt he has a point – his time would be better spent focussing on keeping the ball out of United’s net and keeping himself on the pitch rather than pointing the finger at others.

He has been one of United’s better signings of recent years, albeit one hampered by a succession of unfortunate injuries. The combative edge and winning mentality he brought from his time with Argentina and Ajax have been an asset to Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and, to a lesser extent, Carrick.

Michael Carrick (left) could not say what he really thought but was let down by one of his more senior players

The fans love The Butcher and you can see why at a time when so many players who have passed through the doors during his five years at Old Trafford have failed to show enough heart for the fight

But this was a stupid, selfish act borne out of frustration which cost United any chance of winning this game and will keep Martinez out of United’s last fixture before the international break at home to Aston Villa next weekend.

By the time they return to action, there is no guarantee Carrick will still be in a job.

If you want to compare Michael Carrick’s successful spell in charge at United last season with the seemingly inexplicable drop-off this term, this was exactly the kind of marginal game that he was winning back then.

Think of Carrick’s first two matches in charge against Manchester City and Arsenal, and the 3-2 wins over Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Fulham. Perhaps most relevant of all, the 1-0 win here over Chelsea in April when Matheus Cunha scored the only goal just before half-time.

If United had taken only half their chances in the first half at Stamford Bridge this time, they could have put the game to bed. Amad Diallo had enough of them to win it on his own.

It would be easy to say that Carrick’s luck has run out but it isn’t that easy in elite sport. The confidence that flowed through the team in those months between January and May has drained from his players. Chances are being missed, silly goals conceded. Experienced campaigners like Martinez are suffering from a rush of blood to the head, and every mistake is being punished. That’s what happens when the tide turns and you haven’t got the resilience to ride it out.

Every game looks hard for United at the moment. Their only victories this season have been at home to Sabah and Ipswich, and even the latter came with a slice of luck.

Who knows where their next win is coming from? As he left West London looking rather dazed, Carrick didn’t seem like a man who has the answer to that question.

It feels like Bruno Fernandes's great Manchester United career may be coming to an end

Once we knew Carrick would be in the dugout at Stamford Bridge, all the talk in the build-up to this game was about the return of captain Bruno Fernandes after he was dropped for last weekend’s defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes didn’t just come back into the line-up, he was back at No10 after vacating that role for Youri Tielemans in recent weeks. Tielemans was deservedly left on the bench here while Fernandes interchanged with Cunha in a fluid United attack that performed well in a promising first half.

But the Fernandes of old would have made his mark on this game. Got a goal or an assist to lead his team to victory and ram the taunts of rival fans down their throats.

But he did nothing of the sort. Too many passes went astray, too often the arms were thrown up in the air in frustration. When he had a great chance to put United ahead in the first half from Bryan Mbeumo’s brilliant pass, Fernandes blazed it over the bar.

One man can’t carry an entire team, but the Portugal star has come close to it at times during his seven-year career at Old Trafford. Here, though, was more evidence that his powers may be fading and this United team may be beyond help.

United were open to selling Fernandes to Al-Hilal last year and won’t break the bank to keep him when his current deal runs out in June. They might renew at the right price or at least trigger the 12-month option to make sure he doesn’t leave on a free transfer.

But it feels like a great United career may be coming to an end.

#2208. Farioli in conferenza stampa: “Il Napoli ha preparato la gara in maniera intelligente, match importante”

Francesco Farioli, allenatore del Porto, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo la vittoria in Champions League contro il Napoli:  “Il gioco è stato molto pesante, ci sono stati diversi momenti in cui siamo stati molto energetici e coraggiosi, soprattutto quando siamo andati a prendere la palla e loro ci pressavano, avevamo la giusta mentalità come i tifosi e questo ci ha aiutato ad avere la prestazione avuta. In ogni intervista ho detto che è stata una buona Champions ma non avevamo avuto punti, stavolta abbiamo raccolto i frutti. Questa vittoria è importante perchè ci servivano punti, sappiamo la storia del club e l’esigenza di fare bene in Champions League, di ottenere risultati. Una cosa non si può dire, che ci sia mancanza di volontà: ogni tre giorni abbiamo le giuste motivazioni, ci sono sempre gli avversari e le partite da giocare, e non sempre siamo al top della forma e a certi livelli la pressione si fa sentire. Dobbiamo imparare sulla nostra pelle, ci prendiamo i tre punti contro una squadra eccellente e ora vediamo le ultime quattro partite per guadagnare più punti possibili. La partita di stasera e i risultati hanno cambiato la prospettiva del match, abbiamo dovuto cambiare interpretazione del match e il coraggio dei ragazzi è stato notevole. Siamo stati bravissimi nella verticalizzazione e nel secondo tempo, l’impatto delle sostituzioni è stato fondamentale, chi è entrato ha contributo tanto. Cosa non è andato bene alla fine del primo tempo? In Champions ogni punto conta così come ogni gol può fare la differenza, stasera vincere con tre gol di differenza sicuramente è importante e ci aiuta ad avanzare, la performance dei ragazzi è stata eccellente. Le difficoltà del primo tempo? Non sapevamo cosa avrebbero fatto, avevamo preparato cinque scenari possibili e stasera abbiamo visto le scelte degli avversari con giocatori che non ci aspettavamo in campo. Abbiamo reagito bene e fatto la differenza. Come ho visto il Napoli? Non per dare meriti ai miei, ma il Napoli ha preparato la partita in maniera intelligente, quando ho visto la formazione ho pensato come potessero creare. La prima lettura è stata una scelta strategica e ben pensata in pochi minuti, abbiamo cercato di aggiustare le nuove dinamiche con l’ingresso di De Bruyne sotto punta, siamo stati bravi a portare dentro tanta energia, nel secondo tempo siamo venuti fuori con la condizione fisica e ritmo, chi è entrato ha alzato il ritmo ed è qualcosa in cui credo molto. Ho chiesto a Fofana e Gimenez di giocare fuoriruolo ma hanno avuto determinazione e spirito. Il calcio italiano? Le informazioni sono veloci e si può raffrontarsi con altre realtà, la Serie A la seguo da tifoso e da osservatore esterno, alcune dinamiche le conoscete meglio voi. Nuova onda degli allenatori toscani? Facciamo un lavoro bellissimo quando i risultati vanno bene, difficilissimo se la palla non entra. Spalletti ed Allegri sono dei riferimenti del calcio italiano, hanno portato innovazione nel ruolo dell’allenatore e ho un rispetto enorme per ciò che hanno fatto e continuano a fare. Su Alvini posso dire che è incredibile per lo spirito che ha il Frosinone, tanti anni fa andavo a vedere i suoi allenamenti al Tuttocuoio e ha sempre avuto una grande passione. Mi ha aperto le porte del suo centro sportivo per gli allenamenti e ancora non pensavo di allenare, ha un modo contagioso per come allena. Come abbiamo vinto? A fine primo tempo ho detto di avere ancora fiducia come nei primi 35′ di partita. Abbiamo avuto coraggio e alla lunga abbiamo meritato la vittoria, grande meriti ai ragazzi. Gabri Veiga aveva la febbre, aveva una faccia bianca stamattina e non aveva dormito: quando è uscito gli ho detto meglio fare così ogni partita. Ha grande intelligenza, conosce i momenti della gara e oltre a leggere il gioco aggiunge qualcosa di speciale come la sua fisicità strabordante come volume ed esplosività. Ha ancora grandi margini di miglioramento sulla continuità, sta migliorando e rispetto al suo percorso ha voglia di fare tanto e bene. Poi tra cinque anni chissà, per ora ce lo godiamo. Occasione per un italiano all’estero prima di tornare in Italia? A volte non danno e a volte non si prendono le opportunità, ci sono momenti: negli ultimi due anni e mezzo ho lavorato per club con sale piene di trofei. Lavorare assieme come succede al Porto poi ti rende difficile guardare altrove, sono felice qui: è la realtà, sono felice di lavorare con un gruppo straordinario e con le persone che rappresentano il club e fanno di tutto per il club, creativi nel cercare soluzioni nei momenti di difficoltà. Abbiamo tante partite da giocare, testa bassa e pedalare”.

#2206. Tributes paid after death of Tenerife striker following on-field collision

Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club has announced.

The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier game.

The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

“There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as “stable despite the severity of his condition”.

An update in the early hours of Tuesday morning said his condition had “worsened neurologically”.

Owono was immediately sent off after he charged out of his goal to challenge De Miguel in the centre circle, his knee appearing to connect with the Tenerife player’s head.

Andorra and Tenerife players beckoned on medical staff immediately and appeared visibly upset by De Miguel’s condition.

The match was suspended after the incident.

#2205. Three goals from 1.27 xG: Sydie Peck defies the numbers to break seven-year Sheffield United duck

Sheffield United continued their fine form on Tuesday night as they defeated Preston North End 3-2 away from home. SUFC are now four games without defeat, and they’ve won four of their last six Championship matches.

It was a strong team performance from the Blades, but the man-of-the-match display from hat-trick hero Sydie Peck can not be overlooked. The 22-year-old midfielder scored three in the first half, becoming the first United player to score a competitive first-team hat-trick since Billy Sharp against Aston Villa in February 2019.

Peck did so from an expected goals (xG) of just 1.27 too. First, his cross bounced all the way through and beyond Daniel Iversen (0.02 xG) before he kept the Preston North End ‘keeper at bay and floated beyond a despairing defence for his second (0.21 xG). Finally, the Blades star slid in at the back post to convert from Romelle Donovan’s cross (0.81 xG) to seal his hat-trick.

Peck registered a total of 1.27 xG across his six shots – the most by anyone in the game. His attacking threat was emphasised by the fact his six touches in the opposition box was more than any other player too.

The Sheffield United man saw to his usual duties. He created two chances in total and completed 52 passes, also winning six out of seven aerial duels – a tally bettered by only Mark McGuinness in the SUFC side (Fotmob).

It was the complete midfield performance from Peck, who has grown in influence this season. His importance creatively is displayed by 21 chances created and 76 line-breaking passes, and 779 touches shows how regularly he is the man to get on the ball when the Blades have possession.

Peck has made 54 defensive contributions too though, winning 52 duels in total. This shows his willingness to get stuck in and do the dirty work, while 50 recoveries highlights his work rate as well (Fotmob).

Now on four goals this season, if Peck can start to score on a more consistent basis, he will really be a complete midfielder for Chris Wilder.

Peck has been with Sheffield United for over five years now, joining the academy after his exit from Arsenal. He broke into the team in the 2024/25 campaign and would grow in the 2025/26 season with five goals and five assists in 41 games across all competitions.

The London-born midfielder drew interest from West Ham in the summer, but he expressed a desire to pay back all those who have shown faith in him at Bramall Lane – including manager Wilder.

Peck is happy with SUFC and his continued improvements this season show his development isn’t being impacted by sticking around either. However, if he continues in his current form, interest is bound to grow, and exit opportunities will become more tempting.

Sheffield United are keen to renew Peck’s contract as his current deal runs out in 2028. It would be wise to strike an agreement sooner rather than later with clubs sure to be alerted by his impressive displays of late.

#2202. How much West Ham paid to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after missing the chance to do it for free

West Ham made the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo on Monday, after a 3-1 home defeat to West Brom. WHUFC have acted quickly to hire Scott Parker as their new boss, but they had to pay a sizeable compensation fee to part ways with Nuno.

The Athletic states that the Hammers paid around £2m to relieve the Portuguese boss of his duties. This is after having the option to do so for nothing after their relegation from the Premier League was confirmed in May.

New manager Parker had the support of board members as early as May, before opting to stick by Nuno. Mark Noble was among the 46-year-old’s strongest backers but Dutch coach John Heitinga was also considered as a potential replacement.

As soon as the decision was made to stick by Nuno in the summer, the pressure was on for the West Ham boss. He failed to keep them in the Premier League, but there was hope he could get them back there having led Wolves to Championship promotion in impressive fashion in 2017/18.

There were encouraging signs, as the Hammers rose as high as top of the table during a run of 10 Championship games unbeaten. They scored for fun too, scoring 30 times in the first 11 matches, including big wins over Wrexham, Lincoln City (both 6-0), Derby County (3-0) and Wolves (4-2).

However, frustrations over the style of football continued with cautious play in possession persisting despite WHUFC’s star power in attack. Defensive concerns persisted too, and when the warning signs led to defeats against Southampton and west Ham, the crowd had turned on Nuno.

United are ultimately made to pay for sticking by Nuno in the summer – £2m to be exact. The appointment of Parker for nothing limits the expense of this managerial change, but when the Portuguese boss could have gone in the summer for nothing, it has proven to be a costly decision by the club.

West Ham’s appointment of Parker has led to a mixed response. Many are pleased to see a former Hammers star and three-time Championship promotion-winning manager join the club, but there are some reservations over his style of play.

Like Nuno, Parker’s tactics in recent jobs have been built on a solid defensive foundation, showing a willingness to let the opposition have the ball, and when his sides do have it, playing conservatively.

However, Parker has adapted his tactics over time. While in charge of Fulham, his side had the second-highest average possession in the Championship with 60.8% (Fotmob), and they went on to win the league. They also recorded the highest xG (90.4 – 20 more than any other team), most big chances created (136) and most touches in the opposition box (1,352).

It will be intriguing to see if Parker reverts to this, or sticks by the defence-first tactics that saw him win promotion with Burnley after conceding only 16 goals in 46 matches.

WHUFC supporters want promotion at any cost, but the criticisms of Nuno’s style of play suggest they would rather brings more forward-thinking and controlling football.

#2201. Wesley Fofana has a shot at redemption after shocking first half in Man United win, Estevao cements his status as Chelsea's fan favourite - and why Romeo Lavia was their star man, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 02:01 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 04:27 EDT, 1 November 2026

There is something called the Science of Scare Project.

It is a study ranking the most frightening films of all time by measuring an audience’s reaction to watching them. Via their average heart rate, highest spike, time between heartbeats, and so on.

Halloween enthusiasts consulting this year’s eerie list found the spookiest ever was a 2012 supernatural horror called Sinister. That received a 'Scare Score' of 96/100. It beat The Conjuring (88/100), Paranormal Activity (73/100), Texas Chainsaw Massacre (65/100), and so on.

If only the good folks behind this scientific study had hooked up the Chelsea fans at Stamford Bridge. It would have been intriguing to know the fluctuating activity of their hearts as they watched Wesley Fofana flirt with gifting Manchester United the opening goal.

We would have seen the spikes occur whenever he was involved. Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more while Maxence Lacroix is recovering from his hamstring injury.

Xabi Alonso has told us Lacroix is facing ‘a few weeks’ on the sidelines, but sources around the player have suggested he may not return until 2027. That information has also been stood up by the odd contact at the club.

Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more

Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch Estevao (left) and now he has given Alonso a selection headache

Which is worrying for Alonso and Co. While Chelsea wound up winning 2-0 against an abysmal United team now hovering over the relegation zone, Fofana’s first half was a shocker.

First, he was burgled of the ball by the halfway line. Amad countered, and while he should have made more of the chance, he won a corner. United scored from this attacking phase, but Chelsea survived when VAR decided the scorer, Matheus Cunha, was offside.

Then, Fofana misjudged a long pass to leave Amad with only Mike Penders to beat. Chelsea got away with that one, too.

This followed what happened at Anfield on Wednesday when Chelsea exited the Carabao Cup. Fofana swapped football for volleyball at a Liverpool corner to hand them their penalty equaliser. At the shootout, he was the unfortunate soul who skied the decisive spot-kick to confirm defeat.

If Alonso had any other senior central defenders available on his bench, he might have made the change at half-time versus United. He did not, and so Fofana survived a hooking.

To Fofana’s credit, he calmed after the break. He was the one clattered to win Chelsea their penalty and earn Lisandro Martinez his second yellow. There was even a point towards the end, when Chelsea were leading 2-0 against United’s 10 men, that he was trying to pass from the back.

Bruno Fernandes stood in his way and so he simply nutmegged his opponent to find Valentin Barco. As Fofana jogged by Fernandes immediately afterwards, he rubbed it in a little, laughing at United’s captain with a little finger-wagging gesture.

That told us the confidence is there, though Chelsea fans will continue to fear he is a player too prone to a clanger, rather than a centre back who cost £75million from Leicester City in 2022.

Even before his errors here, there were pieces penned by other websites suggesting he should be seen as the worst signing of the BlueCo era. Thanks to his driving infringements, we know how much he earns, too. More than £200,000 per week, his lawyer had to tell Lavender Hill Magistrates' Court in January as his client reached a remarkable 50 points on his licence.

It is fair to say he has not lived up to the hype which accompanied his arrival with injuries having hampered his career. But here is a small chance at redemption. Lacroix may miss the remainder of 2026, and Fofana will be needed. Chelsea would love him to reduce his 'Scare Score' which, in the first half of this win over United, was rivalling Sinister’s record.

Those of us inside Stamford Bridge did not notice it. We thought Bryan Mbeumo had sent his shot straight into the crossbar. But then we saw Penders celebrating, and the slow-mo replays.

Penders got his fingertips to it. He stopped any chance it had of creeping underneath the crossbar to reduce the scoreline to 2-1. The 21-year-old Belgian earned this clean sheet.

It was good to see. He had a nightmare against Tottenham, there is no hiding from that. He punched a cross into his own goal to give Spurs their opener in that 2-0 defeat. But at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, he responded well. Then here against United, he would not be beaten.

There has been talk of Chelsea rushing back Martinez from his jaw injury, maybe by having him wear a protective mask. But Penders performing like this may mean that is not necessary.

The loudest cheer when the line-ups were announced was reserved for Estevao, followed by Stamford Bridge chanting ‘Stevo, Stevo’. They love him, and they are right to love him.

He had to wait a long time for his first Premier League start of the season. Arguably too long.

But he seized his opportunity. Estevao scored two goals – alas, both were disallowed for offside – but he was forever involved. Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch him, and now, he has given Alonso a selection headache because it was a showing which said he should start more.

Daily Mail Sport reported in our Chelsea Confidential column this week how there had been no fallout between Alonso and Estevao, despite speculation suggesting otherwise. His exclusion from the line-up was down to tactical and technical decisions.

When Estevao thought he had scored for the second time, he ran over to Alonso to give him a hug. When substituted, there was another cuddle. All is fine in that relationship, even if the 19-year-old Brazilian is itching to play more.

Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring

Jordan Henderson fell ill and so was unable to start his sixth successive match for Chelsea.

But that afforded an opportunity to Romeo Lavia. He had completed his first full 90 in a competitive game for Chelsea at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup. Then, a day before this Premier League visit of United, he was told he would need to start again.

Despite TNT Sports being blinded by Morgan Rogers’ fine opener – they gave him the player-of-the-match award – Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring. He then completed yet another full 90. You wait for one bus, then two come along at once.

#2198. Three games, three goals, three wins: Midfield maverick stars again as Norwich City thrash Derby County

Norwich City cruised past Derby County with much of the hard work done by half time. NCFC were 3-0 up at the break, and Jovon Makama lashed home a stunning striker to seal the victory in the second half.

It was another strong team performance for the Canaries, as displayed by the fact there were four different goalscorers. However, one man who stood out and got himself on the scoresheet once again was attacking midfielder Paris Maghoma.

Maghoma had Rams midfielder Alex Mowatt biting on every dummy before he fired home from outside the box for the Canaries’ second goal of the night. It made it three goals in three consecutive wins for the maverick playmaker, who looks to be back at his best.

Maghoma made an impression early on in his Norwich City career, scoring in his first starts in the FA Cup and Championship after joining in January. His trickery and flair has frustrated even manager Philippe Clement at times, but it isn’t easy to curtail someone as expressive and skilful as the 25-year-old.

The attacking midfielder was influential in the Derby County win. Alongside his goal, Maghoma created one chance and one big chance, also completed five passes into the final third (Fotmob).

Maghoma had only started two Championship games before his recent three-game scoring and starting run. His per 90 stats show just how impactful he has been when on the pitch though, offering a creative streak and valuable abilities in progressing the ball through passes and dribbling.

Across his 442 league minutes, the NCFC ace is averaging 2.44 chances created, 6.11 line-breaking passes, 57.83 touches and a 60% dribble success rate per 90. His three goals from 10 shots and just 0.87 xG shows how clinical he has been when given an opportunity at goal too – although that does beg the question whether such goalscoring form will continue (all stats via Fotmob).

Maghoma has been a standout player in Norwich City’s three-game winning run, and there will be confidence that he can continue in this vein. However, both he and the entire team face a challenge in the effort to maintain their form.

The last three games have been against Derby County, Watford and Charlton Athletic – three of the league’s worst form teams. If NCFC are to keep pushing up the table and come good on their promotion ambitions, they have to maintain these high standards against tougher opposition.

A trip to Michael Skubala’s Bristol City marks a step up for the Canaries, but it is another winnable match. It would be a real morale boost to enter the upcoming international break off the back of four wins, and Maghoma’s recent form indicates he will have a key part to play in continuing the run.

#2197. Martin O'Neill and Celtic chiefs given ‘hard but fair’ grilling at recent meeting

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill and senior club figures faced more than two hours of “hard but fair” questioning from supporters at a packed meeting in Greenock.

Around 120 fans attended the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, with recruitment, transfer policy, communication and the club’s ambitions and strategy among the issues raised.

Per Celtic's statement on what transpired, O’Neill was joined by interim chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials for the two-and-a-half-hour question-and-answer session.

Wilson admitted the Celtic hierarchy had been prepared for tough questioning.

He said: “We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.”

Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Europa League rivals make shock decision to sack history-making boss

Furious Besiktas star turns on team-mates ahead of crunch Celtic showdown

Supporters from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs clubs were among those represented.

Nicholson also welcomed the opportunity to hear directly from fans and insisted everyone involved shared the same desire to see Celtic succeed.

He said: “Everyone in the room wants the best for Celtic and that was evident.

“We are grateful for supporters’ input and look forward to continuing to meet with supporters as we work on improving communication and engagement in the weeks and months ahead.”

Celtic say further details on the club’s new Celtic Connect engagement initiative and future fans’ forums will be announced soon.

The Greenock gathering followed recent meetings with the Affiliation of Registered CSCs in Glasgow and the Association of Irish Celtic Supporters' Clubs in Cork.

#2196. Nathan Jones confirms worry over ‘tough’ injury setback for Charlton Athletic summer signing

Nathaniel Chalobah made his first start for Charlton Athletic since the end of August on Tuesday night. However, he only lasted until half time following a crunching challenge from Akin Famewo.

And, unfortunately for CAFC, it appears that the tackle aggravated the thigh injury that kept Chalobah out for two months. Speaking to South London Sport, Nathan Jones said: “He got injured. I think it is the same thing as what kept him out at the start of the season – his thigh.

“We will have the diagnosis, but it wasn’t a tactical decision, we won every game with him at the start of the season and then he got injured. We tried to bring him back – he has trained with us for nearly two weeks so it is not too early. We were always going to give him 55-60 minutes anyway, but I think he has pulled his thigh. It is a tough one again.“

Chalobah’s last start came against Preston North End, a game Charlton Athletic won 1-0. The Addicks won their first three games of the season with the former Chelsea and Sheffield Wednesday man in midfield, but they have not won since.

Chalobah has gained a wealth of experience in the Championship, but he has often struggled with injuries. Previous club Sheffield Wednesday spent large spells without the 31-year-old, and the same fate looks to have hit the Addicks. He played only 31 times in a two-year stay at Hillsborough.

Chalobah’s most notable injury came during his time at Watford, when he had major knee surgery in 2018 and spent a total of 340 days sidelined.

Fears are that his injury struggles are set to persist at CAFC. His influence is clear to see as a strong defensive presence in the middle of the park, but the likes of Conor Coventry, Oliver Skipp and potentially the rarely-seen Timothy Ouma will have to cover in his absence.

In the summer, Charlton Athletic recruited some experienced Championship including midfielders Chalobah and Skipp. However, the former is dealing with injuries, and the latter is yet to win a game in CAFC colours.

They bolstered their forward line with Millenic Alli and Karlan Grant. Grant has scored two goals this season, however, Alli is yet to score and both are being outshone by academy graduate Tyreece Campbell – who has not scored in the last five league matches himself.

The Addicks need more from their summer signings, with disappointment over Chalobah’s lack of fitness and the limited impacts of bigger names like Grant, Skipp and more.

Charlton Athletic have some tough matches on the horizon, with Sheffield United, Wolves, Lincoln City and Blackburn Rovers to play before the end of the month. Time will tell just how long Chalobah faces out, but Jones has to find a winning formula with his available players, otherwise his future at The Valley will be in doubt as their winless run stretches to 11.

#2195. Harry Kane embraces his family during special Ballon d'Or presentation at Bayern Munich - before England skipper MISSES a penalty in chaotic draw!

Published: 06:28 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:29 EDT, 1 November 2026

Harry Kane received a hero's welcome as he returned to action for Bayern Munich for the first time since winning the Ballon d'Or.

Kane was crowned as the best player in the world on Monday night, becoming the first English player to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001 on what was an emotional evening for the former Tottenham star.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded the German side's domestic Treble, while he also captained his country to third place at the World Cup.

And, ahead of Bayern's clash against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday night, Kane received a special presentation at the Allianz Arena.

With both sets of players and match officials lined up on the pitch, Kane was welcomed out of the tunnel while holding his new prized possession in his hands.

Harry Kane presented his Ballon d'Or trophy to Bayern Munich fans and players on Saturday

Kane received a hero's welcome from Bayern fans and his team-mates as he walked out

Kane was also greeted by his family, including his four children, ahead of the match

Bayern's players and fans gave Kane a standing ovation as Land of Hope and Glory played over the stadium's sound system.

The England skipper was serenaded by the home faithful, although some Dortmund fans could be heard to be booing him.

Waiting on the pitch were his family, including his wife Kate, four children, his parents and his brother Charlie, and he greeted them all as he came out.

Kane then took a microphone and addressed the home fans by saying: 'I’m extremely proud to be a Bayern player.

'The support you’ve shown me since I arrived is incredible. I’m extremely proud to present this to you. I hope to win many more titles with you.'

Unfortunately for Kane, his on-pitch return didn't perhaps go as planned as he missed a penalty as Bayern drew 2-2 with Dortmund.

Kane had the chance to mark his honour further after Konrad Laimer had put Bayern ahead, but he smacked his spot kick against the bar.

Serhou Guirassy then equalised for Dortmund, and although Kane assisted Dayot Upemecano's response, which put his side 2-1 up, former Wolves flop Fabio Silva equalised for the visitors in the 89th minute.

Kane addressed the crowd on the pitch where he highlighted his pride at playing for Bayern

Meanwhile, after winning the award on Monday, Kane had made sure to pay tribute to Bayern.

He said: 'Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete, so thank you very much.

'To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy. To all the staff, the we way train and the way you push us, it is a credit to yourself.

'Since I have been with you I have improved as a player, improved as a person and a leader.

'It is an honour to play for Bayern Munich, to represent you is a real privilege and I am glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich.'

#2194. SPFL reveals Rangers vs Hibs final date, time, ticket split and prices

Rangers and Hibernian have been handed a 50/50 split of Hampden for next month’s Premier Sports Cup final.

The sides will meet at the national stadium on Sunday, December 13, with the showpiece scheduled for a 3pm kick-off and broadcast live on Premier Sports.

Confirmed match arrangements and ticket information for next month's 2026/27 Premier Sports Cup final 🏆 https://t.co/Iaq1uil4L4

The SPFL has confirmed the ticketing arrangements following discussions with both clubs and the relevant authorities.

Hibernian supporters will be housed across the South, East and North Stands, while Rangers fans will be located across the South, West and North Stands.

Ticket prices will be the same for both sets of supporters.

The majority of adult tickets will cost £42, with adult seats in the North and South Stands priced at £49.

Concessionary tickets will also be available across the stadium, priced at £27 or £30 depending on the section.

Rangers secured their place in the final by defeating Aberdeen last Saturday, with Ryan Naderi scoring a late winner in the semi-final.

Hibernian booked their Hampden return a day later with a 2-1 victory over Edinburgh rivals Hearts.

All tickets will be issued digitally through the Barclays Hampden app, with both clubs set to announce their respective sales information through their own channels.

It will be only the second time Rangers and Hibs have met in the final of the competition.

Their previous meeting came in the 1993/94 final at Celtic Park, when Rangers won 2-1.

#2193. Sheffield Wednesday transfer update emerges as Dave Challinor faces tricky situation

Sheffield Wednesday remain in discussions with the EFL over what they can do in the January window, although it seems unlikely Dave Challinor will be in a position to make major changes to the squad.

It was a remarkably hectic summer for the Owls after Arise Capital Partners completed their takeover of the club at the end of the previous campaign.

A major squad overhaul followed, but Wednesday were under EFL restrictions in terms of what they could do, so the squad was packed out with loan signings and free transfers.

Nevertheless, they still boast a lot of quality by League One standards, but an inconsistent start to the season meant Henrik Pedersen paid the price as he lost his job.

The Yorkshire outfit moved quickly to bring in Dave Challinor as his successor, and the former Stockport boss is preparing for his first game in charge at Oldham on Sunday in the FA Cup.

Whilst he will be keen on a cup run, the league will be the priority, and Challinor will hope to take Wednesday back to the Championship at the first attempt.

In normal circumstances, the new boss would also have one eye on the January window, where he may want to make a few tweaks to the group.

Yet, as outlined above, the situation at Wednesday is different due to the restrictions, and the Sheffield Star has stated that the club are ‘close to the limit’ in terms of what they can spend.

FLW looks at who entertains the most, and the least, in League One

And, speaking to the same outlet, sporting director Simon Wilson admitted they still don’t know exactly how they will be able to back Challinor in the New Year.

“We’re not 100 per cent sure exactly what it is. We’re constantly in dialogue with the league around the rules and the limitations. We obviously have the ability to change the squad, as anyone does. The window is open and business can be done.

“At this moment in time, Dave has just come into the building, he needs a bit of time to assess the squad and get a feel for which players are going to be the most useful and where we have areas of need. Then we’ll work into the window from that point.”

Obviously, this is not ideal for Wednesday, as most clubs will already be drawing up plans for January, and whilst the Owls may have players in mind, they still don’t know who they can bring in.

Barnsley 0-1 Sheffield Wednesday (after extra time), Wembley, 29 May 2023. Type the surnames of Darren Moore's starting XI. Every player you get drops onto the pitch.

You have 90 seconds. Surnames are enough.

Josh Windass headed in Lee Gregory's cross in the 123rd minute to send the Owls up.

But, Challinor won’t be too worried about that, as he will be focused on improving the players he has inherited.

There is still a lot of talent in the Wednesday squad right now, and, to the credit of the new owners, they have done a lot with the restrictions they were under.

Will Sheffield Wednesday win promotion under Dave Challinor this season? Let us know in the comments below.

So, Challinor will believe he can still get results from the current crop, and it will be interesting to see which players benefit from his appointment.

Then, when January does come around, you can be sure that Wednesday will do what they can, but it seems likely that major changes aren’t on the cards, but that shouldn’t be too much of a problem.

#2192. Leicester City must consider January action over £4m starlet’s loan if game time struggles continue: Opinion

Leicester City brought in Michael Golding from Chelsea for £4m in the summer of 2024 with the hope that he could grow into a first-team asset at the King Power Stadium. He had a strong youth career and a growing reputation at Chelsea, but has struggled to make the breakthrough at LCFC thus far.

Golding is only 20 though, and he’s out on his first senior loan with League Two side Shrewsbury Town. The Foxes will have hoped he could find regular minutes with Gavin Cowan’s side, but that has not been the case.

There are two months until the January transfer window opens, and it will be an important period for Golding. If his Shrewsbury Town loan continues how it has started, he could be recalled and relocated by Leicester City.

Golding moved to Shrewsbury Town late in the transfer window in August. Given his lack of senior experience to date, it was perhaps anticipated that the Leicester City prospect would need time to grow into a role at his temporary home.

However, with over a quarter of the League Two campaign down, Golding has played only 115 minutes of fourth-tier football for Salop. He has been used off the bench in the last two games after being unused against Bristol Rovers and Crawley Town, although that was off the back of an absence through injury.

The LCFC loanee gave a taste of what he can offer with a first senior goal in a 2-1 EFL Trophy win over Everton’s U21s last month. However, other players have been favoured in midfield with all of Tom Sang, Isaac Fletcher, Will Gray and Jay Turner-Cooke finding more minutes than Golding.

As he rebuilds his fitness after an injury, it will be hoped he can gain momentum and find more opportunities. As of yet though, chances have been few and far between in League Two.

Golding has impressed in the Leicester City academy with four goals and three assists in 40 games for the U21s. He has only one first-team appearance to his name but still has plenty of time to maximise his potential at only 20.

However, he needs game time to develop and show how good he can grow to be. If Shrewsbury Town aren’t going to offer him meaningful opportunities, LCFC will have to consider recalling Golding in January.

This is a key season for the midfielder’s future, as he will have only one year left on his deal when his Salop stay is currently scheduled to end in the summer. At that point, the Foxes will have to decide whether to renew his contract, or potentially sell him to recoup a fee.

Golding’s 2026/27 campaign will prove decisive in this. If he can show progress on the senior stage, he could earn more time to fight for a place in Russell Martin‘s future plans.

#2191. James Bree incident in West Brom v Southampton match sparks reaction

Southampton full-back James Bree has sparked a strong reaction on social media following his side's 1-1 draw with West Bromwich Albion on Tuesday night.

With the scores level in B71 after Samuel Edozie equalised early in the second period following Isaac Price's first-half opener, it has been debated whether the Saints defender successfully deceived referee, Josh Smith, who stopped the game for a head injury.

Both West Brom and Southampton have started the Championship season in impressive form, with Tonda Eckert's side still sitting amongst the division's early pacesetters despite being deducted four points due to the Spygate scandal.

Those who are a part of the South Coast club have, this season, been playing the role of pantomime villains, and that was certainly the case at The Hawthorns for those backing the hosts, who are now unbeaten in six successive matches.

Who are the biggest wind-up specialists in the EFL Championship right now? Football League World takes a deep dive...

In what was a pulsating encounter, it is fair to say that Albion were more than deserving of their half-time lead, with Saints' attack leaving Max O'Leary untroubled, before Edozie's 53rd-minute leveller certainly gave Eckert's side a fresh impetus.

West Brom still showed signs that they could take all three points, and after a spell of attacking promise, Bree was seen on the ground without movement, leaving Smith to stop the game, although the Southampton physios were swiftly waved away by the full-back.

Asked about the incident post-match, Morrison stated: "I think, because the pressure was coming from us, he tried to stop the game.

Asked whether Bree should have face further punishment, the Baggies boss added: "We've asked for consistency, so let's hope it comes."

West Brom, of course, saw Aune Heggebo banned for two matches for the deception of a match official in August after his handballed goal on the opening day against Norwich City, which was the first time a player had been banned for such wrongdoing in English football.

As such, Baggies fans are calling for Bree to face a similar punishment.

"Faking head injuries is becoming all too common and requires stronger action from officials. If staying down holding your head resulted in an automatic 3 minutes off the pitch while checked over by medics, I suspect we’ll suddenly see a lot less of it," was the opinion of one Albion fan.

Another Baggies supporter wrote: "Disgraceful behaviour, so obvious what he was doing before ref blew his whistle & then waved his hands to say he don’t need any medical attention so he don’t go off. Ref was very poor all night tho imo. Standard EFL ref."

West Brom and Southampton fans, what are your thoughts on the incident? Comment below!

"Absolutely appalling behaviour - so clear and obvious - should have been booked and EFL need to take immediate action for the credibility of football," was another strong verdict on the matter.

"It shouldn’t be done, but it literally happens in every game of professional football," another comment read.

There is, ultimately, no proof that the Baggies would have definitely restored their advantage, but given the punishment which Heggebo received two months ago, the stance of those associated with the West Midlands club is hardly a surprise.

Bree's decision to go down isn't the only incident which has been heavily criticised in recent days too, with Liverpool legend, Jamie Carragher, slamming Alexis Mac Allister's decision to 'feign' injury after the Argentinian midfielder brushed heads with Arsenal's Noni Madueke in the Gunners' 1-0 win at Anfield.

At present, though, it remains to be seen what action, if any, will be taken.

McGregor returned to Rangers as a coach and is now helping develop the next generation of goalkeepers, including McGuire, who has spent time around the first-team set-up this season.

🗣️ "It's a chance for everyone to go and showcase their skills to a lot of people." Rydnn McGuire spoke to @RangersTV ahead of tomorrow evening's #UYL second leg clash against Dynamo Kyiv at Forthbank Stadium. 🎟️ https://t.co/dzAtggjPPN https://t.co/kA5EgInsvc

“He was probably my generation of Rangers goalie growing up, so I watched him from a young age, and he’s been really good to work with.”

McGuire has combined his involvement around the senior squad with appearances in the KDM Evolution Trophy and Youth League this season.

The young goalkeeper believes that mixture has been important for his development rather than simply training without getting competitive minutes.

He said: “I think it’s critical in what I need just now.
