#2118. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#2117. Doubts had been gathering about Roberto De Zerbi but not now, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, as Crystal Palace's ludicrous acts of self-sabotage prove costly in 2-0 defeat

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:56 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:07 EDT, 1 November 2026

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham have won three games in succession. If that proves Roberto De Zerbi’s prowess over at least two of his predecessors, then he will presumably reserve some thanks to the assistance of Crystal Palace.

On a night when Palace crossed to the north of London, with their manager in grave danger of the sack, they contrived to commit an utterly ludicrous act of self-sabotage in two phases.

The first defined the match, with Jean-Philippe Mateta dismissed after only 13 minutes for a challenge that was as brainless as it was dangerous.

From there, Pierre Sage’s side quickly conceded from a set-piece with the sort of defending that explained why Palace have shipped more goals than any other team in the top flight. That no further damage was inflicted until Jan Paul van Hecke’s second-half header was less reflective of the game than the tally showing 34 Tottenham shots to Palace’s two.

Given Sage’s tenuous grip on his job, and the thunderous face in the crowd of his chairman, Steve Parish, that might prove to be the final straw. If it is, Mateta should at least have the decency to drive him to the airport.

Sage said: ‘I am responsible. I have to find solutions. They have to trust in me because I will give my life for it. If I have one hour or 10 years, I will try my best.’

Archie Gray opened the scoring for Tottenham after 25 minutes to settle the nerves

Jan Paul van Hecke slid in to make it 2-0 and all but wrap the game up for the home team

In the recent past, such doubts were gathering around De Zerbi, but not now, and especially with a favourable run of fixtures on the horizon. Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, his side are finally aligning results with performances, even if this fourth game in an unbeaten stretch was aided so much by the opposition.

There remains an issue with chance conversion – both Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush were underwhelming here, with the slight mitigation that Palace spent the better part of 75 minutes camped on the edge of their own area. Marmoush, who started at No 10 after earlier games on the left and up front, appears no closer to revealing his best position.

De Zerbi’s solution was to direct traffic to the wings and it worked a treat. Mathys Tel, riding the isolated high of his performance against Chelsea, was again sharp. So too Mohammed Kudus. But the real gains for Tottenham in this purple patch have come from the central pairing of Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes.

They cost a fortune to acquire and have taken their sweet time to gel, but that partnership has developed to strong effect. On the ball, they are the tempo setters, and off it they have shaped the press that is key to De Zerbi’s system. They controlled this game.

‘Tonali was unbelievable,’ said De Zerbi. ‘We played with two players more - Tonali (counted) double.’

He added: ‘I am very happy with the performance. (But) if we want perfection we have to be more nasty. If I am No 9 or No 10 I want to score.’

The last sentence is very much the Tottenham riddle – an inability to finish what they start. But those frustrations are now coming from an upwardly mobile situation.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi is banishing the doubters as his team climb the table

Having belatedly entered the top half of the table, Spurs are finally aligning results with performances

For Sage, along with whatever consequences this result brings, the regret will come from knowing his side had looked decent out of the gate.

But the red card eradicated those traces of momentum. Initially, referee Michael Oliver felt a booking was sufficient for Mateta’s studs-up lunge into Micky van de Ven’s ankle, but the VAR suggested an upgrade. On review, Oliver agreed.

Sage’s reaction? He had a look of pure deflation. The tackle was bad enough but the need to make it was non-existent – Mateta was chasing a losing cause in Tottenham’s half against one of the quickest defenders in the league. Dismal.

Naturally, it shifted the game in Tottenham’s favour, if only to the effect of a one-goal lead by the break. As with Mateta’s dismissal, the Spurs breakthrough was avoidable for Palace, with Gray left unmarked at the far post before planting his head on Kudus’s high, looping corner.

The video analysis will do Sage no favours. Kudus’s delivery was excellent, that much is true, but five Tottenham men had gathered at the far post with only three markers – even factoring for the red card, the tracking of Gray was abysmal.

At half-time, De Zerbi substituted Gray, who was carrying a yellow card, and Spurs maintained momentum by creating openings for Tel, Matheus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Solanke.

Palace were being pummelled but survived until Van Hecke’s finish for 2-0. As with the Chelsea win, Fernandes stood out in its creation with an excellent cross, from which Van Hecke powered a header at Dean Henderson.

The initial save was good, but the ball returned to Van Hecke, who was sat on his backside and able to steer his second header past Henderson. Sage could use similar inspiration from the floor.

#2116. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners explore loan move for Real Madrid striker Endrick

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are keeping their options open regarding a January move for Real Madrid striker Endrick, as Mikel Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The Gunners have been in contact about a loan move for the Brazilian. There is also talk of a permanent move. However, Real Madrid are reluctant to let him leave and feel he has a big future ahead at the club.

Endrick has struggled to earn consistent game time at the Bernabeu.

While he is only 20 years old and has plenty of time left to make his mark at the top level, a new transfer away from Madrid could give him a more consistent role.

Arsenal are among the clubs keeping an eye on Endrick ahead of the January transfer window, reports TEAMtalk.

The forward was loaned to Lyon for the second half of last season to get more regular game time.

However, his representatives are said to be open to looking for another move if things do not improve in Madrid.

It seems Arsenal are interested in signing Endrick on loan with a view to making the move permanent. This will give them time to see how he settles into the Premier League.

However, Real Madrid may be in a strong position. They are still loyal to the young player and would prefer to keep him at the Spanish club.

Arsenal will rely on Madrid being more willing to let him go.

The reported interest from Arsenal comes as Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

Endrick would provide variety to an attacking line-up which has been under pressure of late. His age and potential make a loan deal with an option to make the move permanent an attractive option.

There is also positivity from his previous stint with Lyon. He has already been on a loan move from Madrid and has demonstrated that he can make progress when getting regular game time.

Arsenal have previously signed young talents from Real Madrid.

Martin Odegaard came to north London as a young player after failing to make an impact in the first team at Madrid. He then became a key player for Arteta, taking on the role of captain.

Endrick will be hoping to follow a similar trajectory.

There is no suggestion that any deal is near despite Arsenal’s interest.

Endrick remains an important part of Real Madrid’s long-term plans. His representatives are thought to be looking at other options to help his career develop.

This loan deal would provide a solution for all parties. Arsenal would have another attacker to bring in, Endrick would play more regularly and Madrid would still have an interest in his future.

It will also depend on how willing the Spanish giants are to move their stance before January.

For now, Arsenal are in contact with Endrick as they consider a move. The Brazilian’s future may soon become a topic of interest ahead of the winter transfer window.

There will be no live UK television coverage of Chelsea’s return to Premier League action against Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

#2114. Rio Ferdinand disappointed Man Utd didn’t sign midfielder better than Elliot Anderson

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

“He came on and showed PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France,” Ferdinand said.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

Rio Ferdinand suggested Bouaddi’s quality could soon make the midfield position in a packed Manchester City his regular role.

City already have Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among their midfield options, but Ferdinand believes Bouaddi has the ability to stand out alongside them.

“They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily.”

#2113. Arsenal news: Arteta’s side secure landmark victory at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal news, Arsenal have finally found a way to win at Anfield again. Their latest victory owed as much to defensive discipline as Kai Havertz’s decisive goal.

The Gunners claimed a 1-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool, ending their 14-year wait for victory at the iconic stadium. Declan Rice set up their opener as Havertz put the visitors ahead on the 16th minute.

It was a tough afternoon for Mikel Arteta’s side as they were put under sustained pressure by their opponents. The Reds also created a number of dangerous chances throughout the match, especially in the first half.

Arsenal held their composure, and the backline was calm throughout. David Raya made the crucial interventions to keep the lead safe.

They are now three points ahead at the top of the Premier League after Manchester City lost to Brighton.

While the attack has been a key aspect of Arsenal’s title charge, they were put under pressure defensively at Anfield.

Liverpool came out aggressively after going behind. Virgil van Dijk caused problems from set pieces, and Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar from a free kick.

Raya was quick to block Van Dijk’s dangerous flick on and prevent Alexander Isak from capitalising. However, Alexis Mac Allister did head over the bar as Liverpool looked to level the game.

Arsenal were forced into another stretch as Jurrien Timber blocked well. William Saliba and Gabriel helped to limit Liverpool’s chances.

The stats tell the story of how well the visitors defended. Liverpool had 17 shots but couldn’t get one on target.

Liverpool were unable to create a shot on target for the first time in recorded history (since 2003-04) in a Premier League game at Anfield.

Meanwhile, it was the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet in the Premier League at the ground since September 2012. The result was especially important following their Carabao Cup heartbreak against Fleetwood Town earlier in the week.

Whilst they have made a great defensive stand, Arsenal’s two most influential players in the final third made the difference.

Rice won the turnover, drove down the right and played a low cross into the six-yard box. Havertz made his run to the back post and finished to give Arsenal the early lead.

The goal also takes Havertz to 46 Premier League goals, making him the most prolific German in the competition and overtaking former Manchester City midfielder Ilkay Gündogan.

Rice had a huge influence on the game. His performance in the middle of the park helped Arsenal deal with the intensity of Liverpool, and he was named man of the match.

Christos Tzolis provided an important attacking outlet. His pace created chances to ease pressure on Arsenal. He forced an incredible save from Alisson with a late first-time effort.

The win was Arsenal’s first at Anfield in any competition since September 2012 and their 300th away win in the Premier League.

Arteta’s team have had a stellar start to the season, taking 24 points from nine games. They have also proved they are capable of getting results in tough circumstances.

They will now look ahead to their Champions League game on Wednesday against Slavia Prague and then back to domestic action against Hull City.

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

The Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

#2111. Arsenal injury news: Eberechi Eze concern emerges as Bukayo Saka awaits scan

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal came out on top in their match against Liverpool. Mikel Arteta admitted they have a new injury concern to deal with after Eberechi Eze was hurt. Bukayo Saka is also still out for the Gunners as they face two more games before the break.

The 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield means they are three points clear at the top of the Premier League. Arteta will need to be careful with his squad ahead of their Champions League clash against Slavia Prague on Wednesday and home game against Hull City.

Eze was a surprise omission from the starting line-up, despite featuring well in recent games.

Arteta later revealed that the England international was suffering from a problem going into the game. He also praised the club’s medical and performance team for getting him fit enough to be included in the travelling party.

There is some light at the end of the tunnel, with Eze being named on the bench. There is uncertainty over whether he will be available for the trip to Prague.

Arsenal will look to train him to see if he can play against Slavia. However, Arteta’s comments suggest that the issue is significant enough that he couldn’t start against Anfield despite his recent form.

There is positive news on Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori. All three were able to overcome their fitness concerns to start the game against Liverpool and play the full 90 minutes.

The availability of these players provides Arteta with more options as he heads into a busy week. However, he will be keen to avoid any unnecessary risk to those that have only just returned to full fitness.

Saka is still the biggest injury concern for Arsenal as he has failed to play for the last three games after suffering a quad injury in the clash against Bayern Munich.

He was forced off after just 10 minutes of the Champions League draw. He will not be available for the fixtures against Slavia Prague and Hull.

There were concerns that Saka may miss up to eight weeks of action. Arteta hasn’t confirmed when he will be back on the pitch.

The Arsenal manager explained earlier that there was a need to scan Saka again to see how the fluid around the injury was behaving. The medical staff will also want to know if there has been any damage to the tendon.

This will give clearer information on when he will be able to return to play. Until then Arsenal will have to plan without one of their most important attacking players.

Another player looking to make his way back to fitness is William Saliba. The defender has not played this season after aggravating a back issue during his time playing for France at the World Cup.

However, he has avoided surgery and has been back in individual outdoor training at the club’s training ground recently. Arteta says there are positive signs that his recovery is going well.

The club plan for an MRI scan to see how he is recovering. They are hoping to get him back in December, but it has not been confirmed by Arsenal.

It would give Arteta a huge boost to his defensive options. For now he will have to keep monitoring his recovery.

They play Slavia Prague on Wednesday and then play Hull at home on Saturday. This gives them two more chances to build up their position ahead of the international break; however, Arteta will have to consider the latest medical reports.

#2110. 'We must improve': Pocognoli spells out where Scotland have to up their game

Sebastien Pocognoli has told his Scotland players that their grace period is over following his maiden camp, and that they have to produce better displays and results when they take on North Macedonia and Switzerland to round off their Nations League group campaign.

Pocognoli was willing to give his men a little leeway in the condensed four-game sequence that kicked off his reign as manager, given that the squad included many new faces and the players were getting used to the preferred system and demands of their new head coach.

Scotland produced a creditable display, particularly in the second half, as they were unfortunate to be held to a goalless draw during Pocognoli’s first game in charge away to Slovenia, but they followed that up with a 3-0 loss to Switzerland at Hampden after Jack Hendry’s early red card.

They bounced back to beat North Macedonia 2-0 in Skopje, but rounded off the opening round of group fixtures with a disappointing 2-1 defeat to the Slovenians at Hampden.

That has left the Scots needing to win both of their remaining matches to have a realistic chance of qualifying for the playoffs for League A in March, and Pocognoli - speaking as he announced his latest squad - has left his players in no doubt over what he expects from them.

“The first camp was to get to know each other. I saw things in training and in the games, we produced some very good moments. We created a lot of chances, maybe more than in previous years against those types of opponents.

“But the next step is to score more goals and clean up the mistakes we made. Because we conceded goals from nothing. We must try to be consistent in the way we want to play.

“We have a different system, different players and different approach to the game. I’m sure we can shine in that way but we need to make the standard higher and win games. That’s the idea for the next camp.

“We need to improve but every country who started with a new coach in September would say the same. Many players in the first camp took it as a new experience with a new style of play and system.

“That needs a little bit of time, but it doesn’t mean we can’t now ask for more and reach the level we want.

“We now have Che Adams back, Scott (McTominay) back, Kieran Tierney and we’re still missing Kenny McLean.

“These players bring stability. I’m pleased with this selection because we feel we have a good mix.”

#2109. Chelsea make early move for Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

#2108. Arsenal transfer news: Arteta considers January moves for two highly rated attackers

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could have two ambitious attacking signings in mind for January. Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz are reportedly attracting Mikel Arteta’s attention.

Both players have emerged as potential targets as the Gunners consider further changes to their forward line. However, Arsenal may face a battle to prise either youngster away from their current club.

Kroupi is already familiar with the Premier League after making an impressive start to life at Bournemouth. The forward arrived from Lorient and scored 13 goals in 35 appearances across all competitions during his first season in England.

His development was halted by a broken foot in pre-season which required an operation to fix and kept him out of action for around three months.

The 20-year-old has now returned to the Bournemouth squad and has played as a substitute in their last three games. He will be hoping to get more game time as he gets back into full fitness.

Arsenal were linked with a move for Kroupi in the summer. His return to action has reignited interest in the player. A number of other European clubs also understood to be watching his situation.

Kroupi has attracted interest from a variety of top clubs including Manchester United, Tottenham, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

The French Under-21 international has impressed with his goal scoring in his first campaign in England. At only 20 years old, he has plenty of development to do under an experienced manager like Arteta.

However, Bournemouth are said to be reluctant to let Kroupi leave in January. Selling a bright young forward would leave Marco Rose with a tough decision to make.

It could get even more complicated if Alex Scott is also being seriously pursued. Chelsea and Liverpool are both linked with the midfielder.

Arsenal may therefore struggle to convince the Cherries to part with Kroupi during the winter window.

Another exciting option for Arsenal comes in the form of Juventus winger Yildiz. The winger has been linked with a move to North London for a number of transfer windows. He has once again been in the news recently at the end of the summer.

However, the Turkish international has struggled to get going on this campaign. He has only featured once in Serie A and has failed to feature since he suffered an injury.

Juventus have previously shown little interest in letting him leave. Head coach Luciano Spalletti firmly dismissed the prospect during the summer. Indicating that even an offer worth €100 million would not change the club’s position.

However, things could change next season. There are reports from Italy that Juventus may have to sell their star player if they fail to make the Champions League.

The Turin-based outfit are currently sitting in seventh spot in Serie A after just 10 games and are six points away from the qualifying spots.

This means that if they don’t make it into Europe, then it could put more pressure on Arsenal’s pursuit of Yildiz. It could create more pressure on them to raise funds.

Arsenal had a very busy summer with the addition of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier.

But they also missed out on a few big names, such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

Despite this, there is still interest in Kroupi and Yildiz, suggesting that Arteta is still looking to strengthen his attacking options. Both players would bring quality and potential to the squad; however, there are some issues with both.

There are many unknowns surrounding this situation. Bournemouth aren’t keen to sell Kroupi and Juventus aren’t in a great financial position.

This doesn’t mean that either player will definitely be moving to the Emirates but much will depend on what happens at their clubs in the coming months.

#2107. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2106. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2105. Arsenal U19s face tough Slavia Prague test in UEFA Youth League

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s under-19s face a significant challenge when they travel to Czechia to take on Slavia Prague in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday.

The young Gunners have picked up four points from their first three games and will be hoping to build on that in the league phase. Two wins would definitely help their chances of getting into the knockout stages.

They kicked off their campaign with a win against Napoli and put on a great show in a 3-3 draw against Bayern Munich last month.

Those results have left them 18th in the standings, 16 places below their next opponents. With the top 22 teams progressing to the knockout stages, another positive result could prove important for their qualification hopes.

However, Slavia Prague has made a much stronger start and will provide a difficult examination for David Horseman’s side.

Slavia have won all three of their first games in the UEFA Youth League and are sitting in second place. Just behind Real Madrid on goal difference.

They began well with a 2-1 win against French side Lens. They then went on to beat Sabah 3-0 and then put in another strong display against Fenerbahce.

Despite falling behind in Prague, the players fought back to win the game 3-1. The three wins means Slavia are already past the number of points they scored last season in the league stage.

They also advanced to the knockout stages last time, finishing 20th before they faced Benfica.

Mubarak Suleiman put the team ahead twice, but they were pegged back by two goals in the last 30 minutes as their European run came to an end.

This season they have looked like a much stronger team. With a perfect record, they will be one of the hardest teams that Arsenal will face.

The meeting on Wednesday provides an opportunity for Arsenal to get revenge for their heavy defeat in Prague last season.

The two sides met during the 2025/26 league campaign, with Slavia winning 5-1 at home.

Arsenal were three goals down at the break after an own goal plus goals from Bartosz Szywala and Jakub Kolisek.

O’Neill pulled one back after the break, but the home side had the final word as Suleiman and Matej Kotrba scored in stoppage time.

This loss shows how tough it will be for Horseman’s side. Slavia have already proven their attacking prowess against Arsenal and are playing even better in this campaign.

The young Gunners will have to play much more disciplined if they are to leave Prague with three points.

Arsenal fans can watch the UEFA Youth League clash on Wednesday.

It will be streamed via the Arsenal app and Arsenal.com, with the match taking place at the Sports Centre Radotin.

Updates will also be posted here and on the club’s Academy X page.

A full match report, highlights and post-match interviews with Horseman and one of the young players will be published on Arsenal’s official channels.

With them still in contention to qualify for the knockout stages, Arsenal will be looking to get off to a good start. Slavia’s great early start means they will have to play some of their best football of the tournament.

#2104. No case for defence if Neil McCann can't turn around kamikaze Kilmarnock quickly

When Gary Neville’s Valencia side conceded a seventh goal to Barcelona, the camera cut to the Manchester United legend standing in his technical area looking ashen faced, utterly bereft.

As you took in his befuddled expression, helpless to prevent the car crash unfolding before him, you couldn’t help but wonder if he would have the gall to soon be back on the Sky Sports couch, telling others how to do the job he had just so miserably failed in.

Of course he did. And that spell in charge of what, admittedly, at the time, was an absolute basket case of a club, has been used as a stick with which to beat him ever since.

If things ultimately don’t work out for Neil McCann at Rugby Park – and it is starting to look as though that may be the case – I am sure he too will be back in the BBC Sportsound studio before you know it. And rightly so. McCann is an engaging and insightful pundit. The qualities that make a good, entertaining football analyst don’t necessarily make a top-class manager, though.

But then, I would say that. I too am paid to give my opinions on the beautiful game, and the highlight of my own managerial career – about half a season as player/manager of Motherwell Phoenix in the Carluke & District Sunday league – was a solitary 3-2 win amid a barrage of hungover batterings. Take that, Lanark Youth.

It would be massively unfair too and disrespectful in fact to dismiss McCann as a pundit turned manager, given his vast experience in the game as a hugely talented player and his previous managerial stints at Dundee, Inverness on an interim basis, as well as his time at Rangers as part of Barry Ferguson’s backroom team.

However, as McCann himself will know having been part of the Scottish football media set, his performance as manager of Kilmarnock will justifiably be subject to the same sort of scrutiny he used to apply to others, and at the risk of drawing a similarly icy stare to the one he fixed on former BBC colleague Chick Young at the weekend when he asked if McCann was feeling the pressure, any objective analysis would have to conclude that things are not going so peachily at present.

Killie currently sit in 11th place in the table, a point ahead of Hibs, who have a game in hand. Most concerningly, they are shipping goals for fun, conceding 2.3 per game so far this term, comfortably the worst record in the division. They have lost eight goals more than anyone else, letting in 28 across their 12 games to Motherwell and St Mirren’s 20. Their goal difference of -15 puts them seven worse off than the closest side, the Saints again, in that column.

McCann has been round the block often enough to know that the team who ships the most goals over the course of a campaign usually goes down. On only four occasions in the Premiership era have the side who conceded the most goals survived, with two of those doing so via the playoffs after finishing 11th. Never has the team with the worst defence in the league finished higher than 10th, which has also happened just twice.

Surely, stumbling to safety, whether that be through the playoffs or by scraping into tenth place, isn’t the limit of Kilmarnock’s ambitions this term? If they continue on their current trajectory, though, and carry on defending so poorly, then not only will that be their ceiling, it also seems a bit of a reach. Across McCann’s time at the club, in fact, Killie have conceded 53 goals in 22 league games, a record that is surely unsustainable.

It would be remiss not to mention though that many of those games came after he walked into an absolutely dire predicament in January following a run of 10 games without a victory under predecessor Stuart Kettlewell. That extended to 14 games under interim boss Kris Doolan before club owner Billy Bowie sent out the SOS to McCann and assistant Billy Dodds in early January.

Kilmarnock were also 11th at that time, just three points ahead of bottom side Livingston, who had a game in hand. Had you offered any Killie fan the playoff spot at that stage, they might have bitten your hand off like a, well, hungry squirrel, but McCann managed to turn things around despite the make-up of the squad not being suited to his preferred 4-2-3-1 formation, and he secured the Rugby Park side’s safety with a game to spare.

It is fair to say then that the many sceptics who gave his appointment in the winter window a frosty reception were mainly won over by the fine job he did in the remainder of the campaign.

There was a great deal of optimism around in the summer, in fact, that having had the opportunity to build a squad in his image, that the issues such as the leaky defence that had plagued Killie would be ironed out, and all the while, he would retain the front-footed approach that had been so refreshing during his first months in charge.

The balance, though, is still way off kilter. While Killie still look decent going forward at times and play some nice stuff, there is no way of dressing up their persistent issues at the back. Their defending at times is absolutely criminal, and you can't be in a position where you need to score three times in a game just to have a chance of winning.

McCann held his hands up to a naïve approach when Celtic came and plundered four first half goals in an eventual 5-1 win at Rugby Park back in August, but naïve barely covers the way that his team twice gave up a lead against 10-man St Johnstone on Saturday.

The second goal in particular had to be seen to be believed. A Killie corner somehow led, within seconds, to an opposition player running through on goal, with the set-up behind the ball leaving the hosts wide open. Even then, in fairness to the Killie manager, his defenders should have done much better when they got back at Joel Cotterill, but three retreating Killie men allowed him to waltz through on Nico Mantl unhindered before finding the net to howls of derision from the home stands.

And therein lies the growing issue for McCann. The boos are getting louder week upon week. While it could be argued that he deserves a bit of time to correct the defensive issues his team are facing after the escape act he pulled off last season, the more that his side display the same consistent weaknesses, the less faith there is from the Killie support that he can pull their team out of another mess. This time, one of his own making.

In the end, it won’t be his erstwhile colleagues in the media that seal his fate, but those paying – and increasingly, braying – punters. If he doesn’t want to be back at Pacific Quay any time soon, he has to find a way to bolt the back door.

There are no guarantees of course that changing manager mid-season would help pull Kilmarnock out of this death spiral they are currently in. Though, admittedly, it did work for them the last time they tried it.

Time is surely running out for McCann to avoid being on the other side of that scenario.

#2103. Arsenal handed major William Saliba injury boost ahead of Manchester City showdown

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have received a significant boost with William Saliba returning to first-team training. He’s spent almost four months out with a back injury.

The French international was seen returning to training on the pitch. Sparking hope that he could be back in action soon for Mikel Arteta.

Saliba has been sidelined since he suffered the injury in France’s 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain. The defender was forced off after only 30 minutes after playing the full 90 in his previous five starts at the tournament.

The player was confirmed by Arsenal to be sidelined for a lengthy period of time in July. He did not require surgery, meaning he can begin working back into action.

His latest progress comes at an important point in Arsenal’s season, with several major fixtures approaching.

The 25-year-old has travelled to the Czech Republic with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba had played for 45 minutes in a behind-closed-moors game last week as part of his rehab.

He then returned to full first team training on Tuesday, providing another defensive option for the club.

Arteta spoke ahead of the game against Slavia Prague. He said that Saliba is happy with his recovery and is at a point where he will be used if needed.

The Arsenal manager has not confirmed if the Frenchman will be involved tonight.

Saliba has not played in a competitive game since losing to Spain in the World Cup semi-final for France. So it will be his first involvement in a competitive game since the summer.

Arsenal have coped well with Saliba’s absence.

Gabriel initially partnered Cristhian Mosquera at centre-back before the Spaniard suffered an ankle injury. This allowed Ezri Konsa to come into the starting line-up.

Ezri Konsa settled into a partnership with the Brazilian. He joined from Aston Villa for £51 million in the summer.

The partnership has helped the Gunners to have the best defensive record in the Premier League. Having only conceded 5 goals in their first 9 games.

Now that Saliba is available, Arteta has more options and flexibility with his defenders.

The manager has had past success with Saliba and Gabriel as his first-choice central defensive pairing. Their understanding has played a big part in Arsenal’s defensive displays.

However, Konsa has provided Arteta with another selection dilemma to consider when Saliba is back to full fitness.

Arsenal have a busy schedule ahead after today’s Champions League game at Slavia Prague.

On Saturday they play Hull City, followed by games against Manchester City, Real Madrid and Tottenham after the international break in November.

If Saliba can come back in, it will give Arteta more defensive options to play with, but they won’t want to rush him back.

The defender played 50 times last season, helping Arsenal win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final. He also ranked 29th in the men’s Ballon d’Or in October.

His return to training is a major step in his road to full fitness, but it remains to be seen if he will play against Slavia Prague tonight.

#2102. Falkirk 2-0 Celtic: Pressure is mounting on Martin O'Neill as Scottish giants suffer a sixth defeat in 10 matches - as hosts celebrate their first win over Bhoys since 2007

Published: 10:11 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 10:55 EDT, 1 November 2026

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made ten saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in ten matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan is in the thick of it during a scuffle at the Falkirk Stadium

Owen Eames hails goalscorer Scott Tanser after he scored Falkirk's second

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

Celtic captain Callum McGregor looks frustrated during their loss to Falkirk

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

#2100. Ex-Celtic star backs 'amazing' former boss to deliver amid growing pressure

Vidar Riseth believes Celtic should stick with Martin O’Neill and has backed his former boss to mastermind a huge European result against Besiktas.

The Norwegian played under O’Neill during his first spell at Parkhead and remains convinced the 74-year-old is the right man to steer the Hoops through their current difficulties.

Speaking to SunSport, Riseth insists Celtic are fortunate to have a manager of O’Neill’s calibre in the dugout as he urged the club hierarchy to keep faith with him.

O’Neill is under increasing pressure following six defeats in Celtic’s last ten matches and desperately needs a victory against Besiktas to keep their slim hopes of reaching the Europa League knockout stage alive.

But Riseth has no doubts over his former gaffer’s ability to turn things around. He said: “For Martin to come back how he did last season was amazing. And now the best thing Celtic can do is to keep Martin as long as they can, because he is one of the great coaches.

“It doesn’t surprise me he is still going at his age. As long as Martin can talk and can sit in the dugout, he will do a good job because he’s an amazing guy.

Three Celtic summer signings named in B team XI to face Ross County

Celtic vs Hibs moved to new date as a result of Premier Sports Cup final

Martin O'Neill and Celtic chiefs given ‘hard but fair’ grilling at recent meeting

“Straight away, Martin was such a good leader for us - as soon as he came into the dressing room, you just knew Martin was going to be a great coach.”

Riseth experienced O’Neill’s impact first-hand after the Northern Irishman took charge of Celtic in 2000.

Celtic’s European campaign has been a major source of frustration this season, with Riseth’s former club LASK producing a dramatic turnaround to knock the Hoops out of the Champions League.

Their difficulties have continued in the Europa League, where three defeats have left Celtic 35th in the 36-team league phase. However, Riseth insists there is still time for O’Neill and his players to salvage their campaign.

He said: “After seeing the first leg with LASK, I was sure Celtic were going to win. That was one of the most disappointing games I’ve ever seen from Celtic. They’ve still hopefully got enough games left to turn it around in the Europa League.

“They still have a chance, so they just have to believe and keep going.”

#2099. Newcastle United young stars with brilliant win over League Two side to progress for first time in 8 years

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

A great Tuesday night for the Newcastle United young stars as they beat the Rotherham United first team 1-0 at the New York Stadium.

Now renamed the Jersey Mike’s Trophy, the EFL Trophy is a cup competition for all League One and League Two clubs, plus under 21 sides from 16 Category One Academies (Arsenal, Aston Villa, Brentford, Brighton & Hove Albion, Chelsea, Crystal Palace, Everton, Fulham, Ipswich Town, Leeds United, Liverpool, Manchester City, Newcastle United, Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Tottenham Hotspur).

After an excellent 3-1 win away (the League One and Two clubs always have home advantage) at League Two club York City and an unlucky 2-1 defeat away at League One Bradford City, the Newcastle United young stars had to beat League Two Rotherham United to ensure progress from Northern Group C.

It was 17-year-old Kyran Thompson (pictured at the top of this report) who was the match winner, a very clever finish in the 34th minute to round off an excellent team move involving Alfie Seldon and Vakhtang Salia.

Thompson chose to move from Arsenal to Newcastle United this summer and looks a real star in the making.

It was a real team effort though and a very youthful NUFC Under 21 side controlled the game, 16-year-old keeper Roman Dowell made a few saves in the first half but didn’t face a single shot on target after the break.

As well as the winning goal from Kyran Thompson, the Newcastle United young stars went close with a header from Miodrag Pivas. Michael Mills saw a free-kick well saved and the home keeper also prevented Kyran Thompson scoring his second goal.

Rotherham United are currently managed by Alex Bruce, son of our old mate Steve.

This 1-0 victory makes it five wins in a row in league and cup for the Newcastle United Under 21s.

It also means a first time in eight years that the Newcastle United young stars have progressed to the last 32 of the EFL Trophy.

That came in the 2018-19 season and ended up with the hilarious last 16 match where the Sunderland first team had the humiliation of having to play the Newcastle United kids in a competitive match. The Mackems won that game and progressed all the way to Wembley in what was then known as the Checkatrade Trophy, only to lose to Portsmouth in the final.

Newcastle (3-4-3): Roman Dowell; Henry Johnson, Miodrag Pivas, Logan Watts; Matheos Ferreira (Luke Craggs 74), Scott Bailey, Mason Miley (Jayden Kouossu 74), Dylan Charlton; Kyran Thompson (Guy Bloomer 90), Vakhtang Salia (Michael Mills 74), Alfie Seldon (Kyle Fitzgerald 74)

#2098. Cardiff v West Ham Preview: Parker Era Beckons After Nuno Sacking

Cardiff City v West Ham United EFL Championship Cardiff City Stadium Wednesday 4 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

West Ham United’s crucial Championship match at Cardiff City will take place against the backdrop of a dramatic managerial change. Nuno Espírito Santo has been sacked with immediate effect following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion.

Scott Parker is expected to replace him, with discussions at an advanced stage and an official announcement anticipated. However, at the time of writing, West Ham have only confirmed that Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville are preparing the squad for Wednesday night.

The change completely transforms the complexion of a match which had looked capable of determining Nuno’s future. West Ham now travel to Wales looking for an immediate response, a much-needed lift and the first glimpse of what could become Parker’s latest Championship promotion challenge.

Scott Parker knows how to get out of the Championship

West Ham confirmed Nuno’s departure following what the club described as a thorough review of the Championship season. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left, bringing the Portuguese coach’s reign to a complete end.

The decision is hardly surprising after Saturday’s dreadful 3-1 defeat against West Brom. West Ham showed little motivation, lacked a coherent tactical plan and were repeatedly exposed by a team operating with far greater organisation and purpose.

Nuno leaves the Hammers eighth in the Championship after six victories from 13 league matches. We are six points behind leaders Middlesbrough and four away from the automatic-promotion places, which is not an insurmountable position but is considerably worse than expected.

The official statement explained that the board believed change was necessary to keep the club’s objectives on track. That is difficult to argue with because West Ham’s target was never to scrape into the play-offs; it was to secure an immediate return to the Premier League.

The full announcement confirming Nuno’s departure can be read in West Ham United’s official club statement.

Scott Parker is now expected to become West Ham’s new head coach. The former Hammer has been identified as the leading candidate, with multiple reports suggesting an agreement has been reached and only the formal announcement remains outstanding.

Parker’s record in the Championship is the obvious attraction. He has won promotion with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, meaning he understands both the division and the specific challenge West Ham face.

He also knows the club. Parker made 129 appearances for the Hammers between 2007 and 2011, captained the team and won Hammer of the Year in three consecutive seasons.

According to our latest information, Parker’s proposed contract is heavily linked to promotion. He is expected to receive a longer-term opportunity if he takes West Ham up, while the club would retain protection if that objective is not achieved.

The timing creates an unusual situation before Wednesday’s match. West Ham have stated that Noble, Potts and Prenderville are temporarily overseeing preparations, but Parker could still be formally appointed before the squad travels to Wales.

Whether he would immediately take charge from the dugout remains unclear. Even if he does, there will be very little time for Parker to introduce significant tactical changes or properly assess a squad he has not coached.

That means the team will probably have to rely upon a reaction to Nuno’s departure rather than any sophisticated new system. The players can no longer hide behind complaints about the previous manager’s tactics, selections or motivational skills.

This is now an opportunity for them to demonstrate that they are considerably better than recent performances have suggested.

Changing the manager does not automatically correct everything which went wrong against Southampton and West Brom. West Ham remain vulnerable defensively, disjointed in midfield and overly reliant upon Jarrod Bowen in attack.

My preferred formation remains a 4-1-4-1, accompanied by drastic changes. Alphonse Areola deserves an opportunity in goal because Mads Hermansen has not done enough to make himself untouchable.

Joël Veltman should start at right-back, with Airidas Golambeckis partnering Max Kilman if Dinos Mavropanos remains unavailable. Kyle Walker-Peters would play on the left if he recovers from the injury sustained against West Brom, although his fitness remains uncertain.

Soungoutou Magassa should operate as the holding midfielder, providing the defensive protection West Ham have been missing. Lewis Orford and Divine Mukasa would then be free to play ahead of him, rather than being asked to perform roles which do not suit their strengths.

Edvin Austbø and Bowen would provide the width, with Joël Piroe finally receiving a proper opportunity as the central striker. As I argued before Nuno’s dismissal, West Ham need to stop repeating the same selection mistakes.

The managerial upheaval makes an honest predicted XI almost impossible. This is therefore the team I would hand to Parker or the interim coaching staff, subject to Walker-Peters and Mavropanos being declared fit.

Cardiff sit 17th after gaining promotion as League One runners-up last season. Brian Barry-Murphy’s team had been unbeaten in three before suffering a 3-0 defeat at Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday.

The Bluebirds could also have up to eight players unavailable. Gabriel Osho is suspended, while Will Fish, Perry Ng, Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers, Krystian Bielik, Alex Robertson and Isaak Davies are injury doubts.

That does not guarantee West Ham anything, particularly during a turbulent 24 hours at the club. However, it gives the Hammers a very good opportunity to respond immediately and begin repairing the damage caused by consecutive defeats.

The mood around the squad should already have changed. Players who were overlooked or used incorrectly by Nuno now have the chance to impress a new coaching team, while those who had become automatic selections can no longer take their places for granted.

My original prediction was a 1-1 draw, largely because nothing about West Ham’s recent performances inspired confidence. Nuno’s dismissal introduces the possibility of a reaction, but it does not instantly repair the team’s defensive and attacking problems.

West Ham possess more than enough ability to beat a depleted Cardiff team. The uncertainty is whether the players can produce a coherent performance so soon after a major managerial change.

I expect greater energy and urgency, but I will retain my original prediction until we know whether Parker will be in the dugout and which players are available.

Prediction: Cardiff City 1-1 West Ham United

Supporters travelling to the match can find ticket, parking and transport information in West Ham United’s official Cardiff travel guide.

I’m with you on the team you picked. If the team is near that then I will go with a 2 nil win for us.

If it ends 1-1 then Nuno has to go, 1 point from 9 just isn’t good enough. These are now his pick of players, his tactics his team management. No excuses!

The reason Nuno is capable of getting wins against Cardiff and Blackburn is because they are not difficult opposition even for dysfunctional West Ham. Why Nuno gets credit for every win is beyond me. He does not know the meaning of the word team and could not pull one together if his life depended on it. So West Ham will win, the rhetoric will be that all is great again, Nuno will get the credit, and the pantomime will continue. We will give him until the next International break. Why? We will give him until Christmas, and so on. Why? We are paying him millions, isn’t that enough? By then he will have cost us a few more millions due to another season in second tier football. Don’t forget we are skint as well, so the excuse for not signing any quality is already in place. Well, he is doing his best, let’s all get behind him. Really?

I had us down to lose the last two games – which we duly did – & the team is unable to defend capably. Add this to strikers who cannot score & you would be hard pressed to think that we will win this game. But, I think we will – but don’t ask me how !

Cool heads needed at the top. 22 points from 12 games. 2 points required per game for automatic promotion. Currently 2 points under that target.

There ws always a common belief that Scott Parker was the Hammers captain In many ways he was our natural leader but I don’t think he was ever officially captain I think that was actually Matthew Upson

#2097. I said the priority should have been to sit Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes down…

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Back on 17 August 2026, six days before the 2026-27 Premier League season kicked off, I put an article (‘The priority should have been to sit Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes down’) up on The Mag.

I detailed how Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes were the key figures of the past five years. The manager and (eventual) captain leading Newcastle United to what had felt unimagined riches in the decade and a half before the October 2021 takeover.

Eddie Howe at the top of the tree managing his squad, with Bruno Guimaraes the talisman delivering on and off the pitch.

The second half of the 2021-22 Premier League season saw only Liverpool and Manchester City pick up more points than Newcastle United, incredible stuff by Eddie Howe and whilst Bruno Guimaraes was given time by the manager to settle in, once he scored that stunning backheel winner in his first ever start (at Southampton), Bruno never looked back.

The rest as they say is history. The four full seasons saw Bruno Guimaraes and Eddie Howe lead Newcastle United to three top seven finishes, two cup finals, two Champions League qualifications, two top five finishes, a trophy.

The 2025/26 season was a tough one, reaching the last 16 of the Champions League, the semi-finals of the Carabao, fifth round of the FA Cup, but also finishing 12th in the Premier League. Bruno Guimaraes also suffered his first injury of any magnitude when at NUFC, missing a key couple of months from February into April. I think 58 matches for such a small squad and so few real quality players was a real killer, it was mission impossible in reality in my eyes.

Back on 17 August 2026 I stated: ‘If Newcastle United fans thought that the final stages of the 2025-26 season were disappointing, fair to say that what has followed is far worse. For me it is anyway. This summer was always going to be a tough one, especially due to the UEFA SCR impact that very much limited the financial flex Newcastle United would have. Careful management of transfers in and out as well as the wage bill. The 2026-27 season was for sure going to be seriously challenging come what may.’

Now it is two and a half months after I wrote that and fair to say this season is now looking VERY seriously challenging.

Six days before this season starting, I said that because of all those challenges that our club faced, it was: ‘Something that for me meant the huge priority, the absolute priority, should have been for those in charge at Newcastle United, owners and senior staff, to sit both Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes down together and ask them what it would take for both of them to be totally committed and confident of tackling the 2026/27 season together. Our leaders staying and leading the way. That clearly didn’t happen.’

Back on 17 August 2026 I stated the obvious, well what to me felt obvious anyway: ‘I think that quite clearly Ross Wilson had been given far more power. Not a case of Eddie Howe losing all control but clearly a major shift in how the transfer window would be conducted. My belief is that Eddie Howe ended up with far less say when it came to whether players were sold and at the same time less say on which signings should be made. I think he would have still been able to say no to a signing and not have any forced on him, but Ross Wilson becoming the main man running the recruitment show.’

Back on 17 August 2026 I said my belief on what happened behind the scenes was as follows: ‘I think Kieran Trippier leaving was the first big blow. My belief is that Eddie Howe would certainly have been in favour of trying to keep him for at least one more season but the change in how things were done, meant that in my opinion, the club wouldn’t have offered Trippier the same wages and no surprise he walked away for first team football and a two year contract at Wolves. Anthony Gordon was clearly put up for sale long before last season ended and who knows what Eddie Howe thought about that. I think maybe he was accepting that one of his key players had to be sold to satisfy the UEFA SCR situation. The end of May and the end of the season, Bruno Guimaraes heads off to link up with Brazil whilst Eddie Howe takes a well deserved break. Only a couple of weeks later though and the Sandro Tonali to Tottenham claims began.’

Back on 17 August 2026 my view was: ‘I think now that when this all started in mid-June the writing was on the wall for the Newcastle United manager and captain. I believe that with Eddie Howe still in charge and Bruno and Tonali in tandem in the midfield, Newcastle United could have successfully negotiated the 2026-27 season. What exactly would have counted as success is another thing…but to me it would have been relative success that could have been achieved and that now looks a very tough ask with how things have ended up. With the Trippier and Gordon dominoes having already toppled, once Tonali followed…I think Bruno Guimaraes and Eddie Howe were all but guaranteed to fall as well.’

I went on to say in that piece six days before the NUFC 2026-27 kicking off: ‘I don’t think there is anything wrong with the targeting of young promising players as a key part of the Newcastle United plan, indeed that is what Eddie Howe proved so brilliant at, when recruiting the likes of Hall, Isak, Bruno, Gordon, Livramento, Tonali…However, this summer has seen the recruitment even younger than most of those successes under Howe and far greater risks with far less experience behind them, far more likely to fail and far more likely to take longer to reach their full potential. Newcastle United have shifted to a model that sees the Sporting Director far more pivotal in directing the transfer strategy and just maybe it might prove successful against the odds. However, I do think that for especially this coming season it has put Newcastle United at great risk.’

I take no pleasure in saying it but ‘great risk’ is very much how this now feels for Newcastle United.

I understand people debating whether or not Matthias Jaissle is the right man for Newcastle United but what is without doubt, he was handed a very difficult situation, some would say near impossible. That is, impossible to achieve in the short to medium term anything approaching what Eddie Howe did.

Back on 17 August 2026 I stated (and still believe): ‘If there had been a big sit down with Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes in May, maybe things would have been different, maybe nothing would have been different. At the same time though I think without the pair of them being at the heart of the plan going forward, it massively helped ensure they would both leave. Eddie Howe came back in early July ahead of pre-season and informed the club he would be leaving, volunteering to hold the fort until a replacement was ready to come in. Which turned out to be Matthias Jaissle.’

Speaking of things I still believe to be true.

On 17 August 2026 I said: ‘I don’t buy into this attempt to make out Bruno Guimaraes to be the big bad guy of this summer. I still don’t know what he has done wrong apart from inform the club he wanted to leave? Everything else is smoke and mirrors with talk of a super agent brought in to help get a move and so on. By the same token the Newcastle United hierarchy were clearly quite happy to move out Trippier, Gordon and Tonali for financial reasons, so Bruno Guimaraes can hardly be blamed in my opinion, when he chooses to follow them out as well. The idea that the NUFC owners and senior staff thought that moving these key players out would then still see both Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes up for staying, is straining credibility. The Newcastle United owners believing that, is on a par with when we had the farce of Alexander Isak going on strike throughout summer 2025 and the NUFC owners doing nothing to sort it. Then believing they could turn up at the very end of the window, go round his house and suddenly convince him to change his mind!!’

My article on 17 August 2026 ended with: ‘I hope for the best this coming season but fear the worst. If the worst does happen, I certainly won’t be pointing the finger at Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes if it all goes pear-shaped. The Newcastle United owners have to step up belatedly and produce a cohesive long-term strategy to properly progress the club. If they don’t do that, we will have a lot more to worry about than what happens this coming season.’

Writing this now on 4 November 2026, not a great deal has changed for me.

I am still not pointing the finger of blame at Eddie Howe or Bruno Guimaraes.

My opinion is that the Newcastle United owners wrecked summer 2025 after Eddie Howe had just delivered the most successful NUFC season in living memory for most of us. A huge dereliction of duty in having no actively working Sporting Director or CEO in place, leaving Eddie Howe totally unsupported and no senior staff in place to help ensure the key Howe transfer targets were delivered. The NUFC owners insisting they wouldn’t sell Alexander Isak and then at the very last minute doing a u-turn and the rushed end of window recruitment of Woltemade and Wissa (rather than the likes of Joao Pedro and Hugo Ekitike who Howe had wanted) made what turned out to be a 58 game 2025-26 season with such a small squad an impossible job for Eddie Howe, rather than just very difficult.

Whether it was intentional or not, the shift by the Newcastle United owners in making Ross Wilson the main man then directly led to Eddie Howe leaving. Also ensuring that Bruno Guimaraes was going to be leaving as well.

What happens next at our football club remains to be seen.

As always with Newcastle United I am hoping for the best but fearing the worst.
