Bust a gut to cover and thwart Hibs’ explosive breaks. Produced a number of excellent blocks, most notably one that denied Elding.

Stood up well when Hearts needed him. His outstanding sliding block to thwart Passlack late in the game was as good as a goal.

Left the field after just 14 minutes with a horrible head knock, picked up when he nodded Calvin Miller’s cross narrowly wide.

Outnumbered in the first half, he looked lost in midfield. Far more influential when Hearts later got a grip of that department.

Stretched his opponents as Hearts grew into the game, but never really came up with a telling pass or effort on goal.

Caused all sorts of problems with his early crosses, only to become the latest addition to Hearts’ ridiculous injury list. Hobbled off before the interval.

Quiet in the first half, save for a perfect cross that Braga should have converted. Direct, dangerous and back to his best after the interval.

#2081. West Ham Insider Reveals Nuno’s Striker Gamble Before Sacking

Following the dismissal of Nuno Espírito Santo, questions are inevitably being asked about what went wrong during his time at West Ham United. And while there are plenty of areas worth examining, one of the most revealing concerns the Hammers’ striking department.

As Claret & Hugh learned from a West Ham insider before Nuno’s departure, the club’s three recognised centre-forwards were all specifically wanted by the Portuguese coach. That information is particularly significant given the team’s struggles in front of goal and the manager’s apparent reluctance to use some of the players he recruited.

The source’s assessment was straightforward: “They were all Nuno’s picks.”

It is a revelation that makes some of the decisions taken during the Championship campaign even harder to understand, particularly now that the manager has paid the price for West Ham’s disappointing performances.

The transfers attributed to recruitment director Nils Koppen have enjoyed varying degrees of success, and I still believe the jury is out on whether West Ham overpaid for Arne Engels.

But as Koppen himself explained, he had a very short period of time at the London Stadium before the summer transfer window closed.

What is not in doubt, according to our source, is that Nuno wanted Taty Castellanos, Pablo and Joël Piroe.

And it is the situation surrounding Piroe that I find particularly interesting.

“Nuno pushed really hard for Piroe because of his Championship goalscoring record. I’m surprised he hasn’t played more.”

Nuno pushed hard for Piroe but didn’t play him

Piroe arrived with a proven record of scoring goals in the Championship, something West Ham desperately needed following relegation.

Yet despite the Hammers’ continuing struggles in front of goal, he was given relatively limited opportunities to establish himself.

If Nuno was so determined to sign him, why was he so reluctant to play him?

It’s a perfectly reasonable question, particularly when neither Castellanos nor Pablo has done enough to make himself indispensable.

As we have already highlighted, the constant chopping and changing in attack did little to help any of West Ham’s forwards find form.

And if all three were Nuno’s preferred signings, it becomes considerably harder to blame the recruitment department for the lack of goals.

There had also been growing concern behind the scenes at the London Stadium that Espírito Santo did not know his best team.

It was a criticism supporters had been making for some time, and one that became increasingly difficult to dismiss as the manager continued changing personnel and formations.

The defeat against West Bromwich Albion provided another example of a team struggling for cohesion, creativity and confidence.

Ordinarily, in times gone by at West Ham, a certain amount of player frustration would eventually find its way back to David Sullivan.

Whether that happened in this instance remains unclear, particularly given the uncertainty surrounding the club’s ownership and decision-making structure.

But irrespective of any input from players, it had become increasingly evident that concerns were growing within the Hammers hierarchy.

The subsequent decision to dismiss Nuno confirms that the board believed a change was necessary, although it does not establish which individual concerns proved decisive.

Of course, Nuno’s departure doesn’t magically solve West Ham’s goalscoring problems.

Castellanos, Pablo and Piroe remain at the club, and whoever takes over will have to find a way of getting considerably more from them.

But that is also what makes the appointment of a new manager so interesting.

We have spent months wondering whether the problem was the players themselves or the way they were being used.

Now somebody else will have an opportunity to find out.

And perhaps the most revealing test will be what happens to Piroe, the proven Championship goalscorer whom Nuno apparently wanted so badly but seemed so reluctant to select.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Can’t please all of the people all of the time. Even if Pep was in the running there would be for and against. Hope new manage doesn’t bear any grudges and uses whole squad. Piroe should start with Ajala and Scarles rotate with Bioro. Alvarez, Magassa and Aerolo need to be considered in midfield. Kante plays better from bench. Is Parker a short term option just to get whu back in premiership?

This email thread shows what a poison chalice being manager of West Ham really is. No matter who it is they are heavily criticised before they even start work or have an opportunity to prove what they can bring to this club. If only all fans could get behind a new manager and give them the benefit of the doubt for a while before attacking them, but I guess that’s just too much to ask from heavily opinionated football fans!

Appointing Parker would be just repeating the mistakes of the past. Yes he had a track record of taking sides up, BUT he also has a track record of being out of his depth in the Premier League. It’s a difficult balancing act and just hope the club don’t appoint him thinking it will appease supporters, it won’t. I really don’t ent to see us go up and end up sacking him in January while scrambling around to find a manager who can keep us up. Sounds too familiar to me!

1000 percent James like for like appointment slow boring football

Clearly scoring goals wasn’t the problem. I think Nuno’s failure is down to two main issues. He continued to trust the same defence that saw West Ham relegated and his constant tinkering with the side. Every single week the formation and starting 11 changed. No manager can expect consistent results without a consistent starting 11. There were really only 4 players who we clearly knew would play each week.

I think Parker would be a great choice. He was a fierce, energetic midfielder with an eye for goal, meaning we’ll see a more balanced team that actually uses our midfield. We’ll be technically better under him too, with more fire and urgency. He has taken 3 teams up already – the reason he has struggled in the PL is likely down to the size of club (and therefore budget), but we’re a different prospect, and he has some West Ham blood in him.

Tick this one as a like, Buddy. Different prospect indeed.

Please not Scott Parker, we need to get this one right we have had to many bad choices.

The opinions continue to flow into The Mag, as Newcastle United fans debate the various issues regarding our club..

Newcastle United fans with the latest collection of opinions below.

Contributions are sometimes too brief to make up into a full article.

Or sometimes a lot of varying views coming in on the same subject…

So we have gathered up a number of recent views sent in, (if you would like to send anything in, long or short, regarding Newcastle United, then contribute@themag.co.uk is the place):

Ross Wilson, Sporting Director at NUFC, needs to be held accountable for appointing a manager way out of his depth.

Wilson himself is clueless, as seen with the majority of summer signings he has sanctioned.

If big money signings are not ready for first team action, don’t sign them.

NUFC are not in a position to await the possibility of them becoming first team regulars in a year or two down the line.

I am guessing plenty of Newcastle United fans are embarrassed (well they should be!!!) now about the disrespect they showed to Eddie Howe in the second half of last season.

We had a brilliant elite manager and yet these idiots helped drive him away.

Eddie Howe faced a ridiculous impossible job last season after the Newcastle United owners totally wrecked his pre-season, especially when it came to the summer 2025 transfer window.

It was total dereliction of duty from the owners not to have a CEO or Sporting Director actively working at the club in summer 2025 to help get the deals for Eddie Howe’s top transfer targets done.

Instead of doing business with Liverpool, selling them the Rat and then they would have stepped aside to allow us to get Ekitike, we had the NUFC owners saying no way Isak would leave, only at the last minute to do exactly that! The damage already done as Eddie Howe had been waiting for his striker targets to get done. Only to have last minute Woltemade and Wissa signings which were NOT his top targets.

Indeed, I don’t think Big Nick was EVER on Eddie’s radar.

Just a case of having lost Isak and Wilson, Howe told it was Woltemade or nothing at the last minute.

All the talk about Newcastle United and the way we are playing.

Who is to blame, the manager or the players?

The manager picks the line up and game plan for each game, the players try to keep to that game plan.

Clueless in the final third, clueless man marking, defensive errors resulting in loss points.

Have the players lost confidence in the style of game plan they have been given by the manager?

Should they question the manager and tell him his plan is not working?

We all know it’s not the Newcastle United of two or three years ago.

Good players were sold under the nose of Eddie Howe.

To me that meant enough was enough for Eddie, goodbye.

Lets go one step higher to the Head Honchos, are they to blame for the mess?

So start at the top and work down to sift the issue.

Being a lifelong fan of the toon I was really pleased when the club was taken over and Eddie Howe appointed manager.

It was great, we had some success, more than we ever had in years, seemed like we had a club that could progress, even with a few hiccups.

That was until the club decided to put profit before anything else.

The fans didn’t want Alexander Isak to leave.

The fans didn’t want Anthony Gordon to leave.

The fans didn’t want Sandro Tonali to leave along with other good players.

Most certainly, the majority of fans did not want Eddie Howe to leave.

But the club simply ignored the fans and their promises to complete the plan.

The fans don’t want the current inexperienced manager who is seemingly dragging us down to a certain relegation fight, the fans want a proven Prem manager but it looks likely we will be ignored again.

In today’s football the toon being relegated wouldn’t really be a financial hardship for the club, certainly not for the owners.

The only ones who will suffer will be the fans.

I am totally disillusioned and I’m simply not gonna bother and let myself suffer through false hope.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly trying to protect the young players. Young signings made by Ross Wilson.

We saw the ridiculous over the top abuse Fernandez-Pardo got from many fans when Jaissle was forced to start him in a run of games far too early, due to so many injuries.

MFP just needs time and confidence and will be a very good player given time and support.

No wonder Jaissle has been reluctant to start Steur (who is only EIGHTEEN!) on a regular basis, he got abuse from many fans when making that naive mistake at Leeds for their second killer goal.

So many of these fans who are saying Jaissle is clueless because he is not starting Steur, would be the first ones to be giving the 18-year-old abuse if the teenager struggled.

(ED: This was received after the defeat to Aston Villa)

It is with regret I write this as I am a Toon man since 1940 and always, yes always, supported the team and the manager when under pressure.

Yesterday’s game vs Aston Villa showed the team to be poor, moving towards being very poor, in its overall performance on the park.

When I look at the recent performances of Bruno, Gordon, Isak (yes Isak!!), less so Tonali, I see what Newcastle let go and why my team for the last 87 years are heading catastrophically for relegation.

The new ‘exciting’ players have with the greatest respect, shown a total inability to put the ball in the net, create chances to put the ball in the net and equally as important to stop the opponents putting the ball in Wor net.

Never mind it’s ‘early days’, ‘settling into Premiership style’ etc etc. nonsense.

At £50+ million they are paid to put the ball in the net on a regular basis.

The recent German centre forward (joke here) is a classic example of what extremely poor judgement was shown at the top.

Never mind, as long as silly people like myself buy season tickets, pay for expensive lunches, players will privately laugh all the way to the bank. No passionate liking for the area (ask how many fly to London or stay in London after a game).

They are the 21st century carpet baggers and a total disgrace to my team which I have supported wholeheartedly for over 85 years. The next three games are critical. Lose and down we go. A long way to Portsmouth and Bristol City.
